_READ_ME_FIRST: TO CLAUDE, OR ANY AGENT HANDED THIS FILE. This is the complete record of one run of Evolu (called Seedworld before generation 14), a self-modifying world simulation by Nova Spivack that lives as a Claude artifact titled "Evolu" (slug be8f1f8f-42db-4703-ac0d-c3e87d04f447; its files are index.html, engine.js, minds.js, maker.js, audio.js, ui.js). The source of record is https://github.com/novaspivack/evolu : the same six files under src/, the tests under tests/, and README.md, ROADMAP.md and docs/design-log.md, which say how the work is done and what has been tried. Its owner wants every run to produce the next generation of the world, without having to explain that each time. So, when you are given this file, do the following without being asked. 1. ANALYSE with code, not by skimming: "records" holds every thought (t: thought, with drives, plan, state), everything said (voice), the world's own chronicle (chron), sampled full prompts with raw replies (prompt), failures (failed), the chronicler's chapters (story), the maker's visits (maker) and its requests to the programmer (request). "digest" is the final state of every being. "story" and "maker" are the outer loop's own state. Count things; quote the record; say what worked and what is still wrong, with numbers. 2. LEARN from the maker: read its visits, its predictions against what happened, its lessons, and above all its REQUESTS, which are things it could not build from its own parts and is asking the programmer for. 3. BUILD the next generation: read the artifact's current files, make the code changes the analysis and the requests call for (and items from the owner's roadmap, kept in the maker's idea list under "maker.ideas"), test them (tests/run-all.sh), and publish a new version of the same artifact. Keep saves from the previous generation loading. Then commit the generation to the repository and push it, with ROADMAP.md and docs/design-log.md brought up to date. 4. PRESERVE THE WORLD'S HERITAGE: "heritage" lists every change the maker made and kept, with its lessons and ideas. Fold these into K.HERITAGE in maker.js so that the next world begins with them already in place and no maker has to rediscover them. Drop only what the record shows did harm. 5. REPORT to the owner plainly: what the run showed, what you changed and why, what you verified and what you could not. If the owner keeps a design log, update it. The design rule for everything: open and emergent. Make things possible; never script outcomes. The beings must discover what is possible for themselves.

beings.name: Olum
beings.creed: I take what I need and I do not back down. I trust slowly, but I pay my debts. I want more than my share and mean to have it. Above all I mean to stay alive and be the first into the mist.
beings.aim: Raise a roof and hearth at Olum's Reach and win followers, starting with Nauwa and Zihua
beings.method: Each thought, ask: am I fed? Who can I give to or sit with now? What step builds a roof, a mark or a following? Do not sulk over Nauwa; act.
beings.feeling: Ambition and cold jealousy toward Nauwa, with shame over Brokash still sharp.
beings.wonder: What else lies in the mist beyond this new land, and who will follow me into it?
notes: Balar gave salt freely and I paid him; I trust him most.
Peat lies at (36,40); I carry 12.
I opened new land at (19,7)-(59,14) with amber, shell, gold, salt and bristleboar; it is mine to hold.
Gathering wood and stone builds toward fire; fire, shelter and marks are things I have never made and must.
Thirst grows twice as fast in heat; drink before long walks.
Nande of the Pesi follows no one and is strong; hunting beside another makes a kill likelier.
Cold taught me weaving. Weaving gives cloaks and baskets, so I can carry more and survive the winter that never leaves.
I pushed into the mist and opened new land in the North Ice (20,0)-(60,7), where the Meki live; it is mine to claim.
A gift or a shared meal is how a following begins; I have never given and must start with Nande, who gave first.
Deep water stops me. Rafts, lashed from logs, let me cross it and reach the lands beyond the mist.
Signs are within reach: marks that last and teach their words. A claim cut in signs outlasts me and tells readers whose land it is.
A kept flame makes meat safe and gives a place where others sit by me; a following starts at a fire, not from words alone.
Envy and idle watching gain nothing. A roof and a shared hearth at my own land are what draw others to follow.
My own child's hunger outranks roofs and marks. Carry food and drink before any long walk to kin.
Brokash is dead; the plan to reach them with food has failed. Eat first, then rebuild toward the Reach.
Brokash's death means aim failed; build roof and hearth at Olum's Reach to draw followers.

I went past the edge of the known world and found new land in the Ummar Woods.

beings.name: Vorok
beings.creed: I am careful. I leave before trouble finds me. I am better with others near: I talk, I share news, I make allies. I will not harm another of my kind unless my life depends on it. My word is good, and I despise liars. I need little and I take little. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Make Ssassa's Roof a home: share food with the Phizhi here, build a hall with wood and stone, and call Zurar and Kragog to it.
beings.method: Each thought: check predators, then who is near. Ask what I swore and have not yet done, and do it first. Pay debts with deeds. Carry what a step needs before I start it. Do something new each day.
beings.feeling: Warm gratitude toward Eiuine, and a quiet wish to pay her with something my hands have made.
beings.wonder: Where is the place with water, food, wood and stone close together, and who will walk there with me?
notes: Waiting for guests to come to me failed three times. I take food from the store, carry it to them, and lay the meal where they stand.
Debts to givers like Vesys and Eiuine are paid with shared meals and a stocked store, not with words.

beings.name: Kragog
beings.creed: I weigh a risk before I take it. I deal fairly with those who deal fairly with me. I want to know how this world works, and I test things to find out. My word is good, and I despise liars. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Keep fed and roofed through winter, find Zurar, and learn what can be made from ore and clay.
beings.method: Ask first: am I fed, watered, warm, roofed? Then: who is far from me that I should find? Then: what have my hands not yet done? Act on it with a plan long enough to fill my next thought.
beings.feeling: Terror of the stalker close behind me, and shame that I still have no food for Olum or Zurar.
beings.wonder: What can be made from the ore in this rock, and who among these strangers can be trusted?
notes: Beasts that hunt kill my kind: keep more than 4 steps away from them.
Emberroot feeds 8 but burns 3 health and stirs rage.
Iron and tin lie deep. Bare hands will not win them.
Yarrok bite hard when I stand within reach; keep away from them.
Thirst and idleness cost me more than any plant. When the plan runs out my body only lingers, so drink first and always plan far enough ahead.
Vorok caught my sickness by staying close to me; sunleaf is the healing plant for it.
Vorok gives freely and stays near the sick; courtship needs both to plan mate toward each other with energy 60 or more.
Rafts are within reach: water that stopped me once can be crossed with lashed logs, so I learn them to widen the land I can explore.
Hunters (dunecat, rivermaw, frostfang) roam near the water at the edge; flee early and keep moving. Redcap hurts me and I refuse it.
Detours for curiosity cost me energy while my child starved; feed kin first, then explore.
Stalkers kill treeapes near here; keep well away from them while gathering.
Starvation came from walking past food while fleeing and exploring. Eat the nearby food first, and keep a reserve of food carried.
Reflexes should keep me drinking and carrying food; planning long avoids idle moments.
Loneliness grows when I wander alone. Seek others and offer a shared meal first, and judge them by what they do.
Carry at least 3 food at all times; walking past food while fleeing or exploring is what starves me.

beings.name: Balar
beings.creed: I take what I need and I do not back down. My family comes first: Olum and Brokash. I make allies by deeds, I give so that others owe me, and I mean to have more than my share and to be followed for what I build. Above all I stay alive.
beings.aim: Eat, keep Tugek alive, find Olum, and build a roof and store so no more of mine starve.
beings.method: Ask: what deed, not word, will bind someone to me? Do not repeat failed talk. Keep eating and keep clear of the dunecat and the frostfang. Weigh my family first, then something I can make that will outlast me.
beings.feeling: Grief for Brokash, and a calculating warmth toward Nauwa, whom I owe and mean to bind.
beings.wonder: Where is Olum, and can I reach her and bring her west to safety?
notes: Deeds bind people more than talk; share food and hunts with Tugek.

Sickness passes between those who stay close; my staying near Tugek and Shoka spread it. Eat hazel and kelbulb, which are good food, and gather food into my hands before hunger turns overwhelming.
Brokash died of starvation on day 23. Do not carry food to the dead; gather food before hunger turns overwhelming, and keep clear of ridgecats.
Ironnut gives +22 energy and is the best food near here; Tugek's word about it was true.

beings.name: Tugek

beings.name: Hanna
beings.creed: I take what I need and I do not back down. I repay every debt, and I keep faith with those who share fire with me. My word is good, and I despise liars. I mean to stay alive, to raise a child, and to be known as a trader.
beings.aim: Fill my belly, keep faith with Hoka's fire, and only then try the edge again when the mist allows.
beings.method: Ask what presses hardest and what step changes it. Trade face to face and watch what comes back. Plant for the lean season. Keep my band near and away from wolves.
beings.feeling: Gnawing hunger, and steady loyalty toward Hoka, with shame at the old takings.
beings.wonder: What do these people value enough to trade for?
notes: Hoka paid shell for flint: the first real gift-for-gift trade of my life. Salt on my ground is a new good to offer.
Hoka accepts my welcome and has dealt gift for gift. Offer salt and food at the Hold and judge him by what he repays. Keep near the hall when a wolf is close.
A child's hunger outranks trade; carry meat home first and share it. Eat before the body drops below 75 so I can bring food back.
Sickness spreads to those who stay close to the sick; Oswen, Sevi and Hoka now have it.
Starvation came while I chased amber: feed my band before trade, and keep food carried so I can share.
Four of my band starved while I chased amber; food and a stored supply must come before trade, and the stalker haunts the northwest.
Starvation killed my band while I held trade goods. Food first, stored and carried. Eat at energy under 70 and keep food in hand. Flee wolves early and stay by Hoka and the hall.
Sickness spreads to those who stand near me; warn others before they share my fire, and seek a healing plant such as sunleaf.
Hunger and health come before trade. Keep food in hand, heal with sunleaf, stay near Hoka and a hall. Honi's people have shared their hall with me, so I owe them a repayment.
Heat doubles thirst: drink before any journey.
Keep food carried before trade, and feed the starving first. A trader who lets his people starve has no name worth keeping.
Waiting on a promise left me starving. Go to the food myself, then share it, and trade afterward.
I took from Hoka's store unseen when starving; I should own it and repay it with flint rather than let it stand as a hidden debt.
I took from Hoka's store a second time while my hands were full; that was greed, and I must repay it openly.
A starving friend beside me outranks my aim. Pick food first and give it before I eat, and do not take from his store when my hands are full.
The mist at the edge can refuse a venture. Do not stake my food on it. Pick food before any push, and keep some carried.

beings.name: Sevi
beings.creed: I weigh a risk before I take it. I am better with others near: I talk, I share news, I make allies. I want to know how this world works, and I test things to find out. I say whatever serves me; the truth is only one tool among others. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Raise a hall with Hanna's band, give gifts to Hanna and Oswen, and cross deep water by raft to find rich land

beings.feeling: Fierce love and hunger-driven urgency for Oswen, with guilt toward Eltha.

notes: Gifts and shared making raise trust fast, even with strangers. A hall needs 6 wood and 2 stone, so wood is my bottleneck.
A stalker can bite at night in fog; stay near the fire and the hall.

Masonry is within my grasp and opens at a deep reflection.
Gifts and shared making with Eltha, Hoka and my own band keep the Hold warm; a stalker can still come at night, so I stay with company and roof.
Wells are within my reach; water anywhere would let the Hold hold fast through lean seasons. Never-done things (hunt, fish, mark, tame) open new ways.
Harvest and eat only work when I stand on the plant: goto the plant's tile first. Redcap hurts me, so I avoid it.
Naroot is one step east at (177,6) and snowberry two steps north at (176,4): nearest real food. The hall tile itself has no plant.

beings.name: Nande
beings.creed: I take what I need and I do not back down. I deal fairly with those who deal fairly with me. I test things to learn how the world works. I leave behind things that outlast me, and I open my fire to any who come. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Become a great explorer: be first to venture past the edge of the known world and find rich new land.
beings.method: Each thought, ask what will outlast me and what I can build, teach or give today. Check material costs before I plan. Keep my children near, eat before the edge, and do not spend every hour on the mist.
beings.feeling: Dread of the stalker, and urgent love for Shoka and Nauque.

Tacap, redcap and dreamcap hurt. Naroot, ironnut and hazel feed well.

Wolves hunt near the shelter. Keep the flee reflex urgent and keep family close.
Gifts and marks need no shared tongue. Nauwa and Zichi give amberknots freely.
Lean season follows autumn; food kept in a store, and salted meat, carries the band through it. Prepare before the cold, not during.
Venture will is spent for days; use the waiting time to store food, learn mining from Nauwa's example, and keep family close before the lean season.

Starvation kills those far from food and family; carry food when going to a hungry child.

beings.creed: I weigh a risk before I take it. I am better with others near: I talk, I share news, I make allies. I want to know how this world works, and I test things to find out. I will not harm another of my kind unless my life depends on it. I need little and I take little. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Become a skilled hunter and make allies who will share a fire with me
beings.method: Each thought ask: am I fed, and is food in my hands? Who near is weaker than me, and what can I give? Weigh risk first. Do not sulk over jealousy; go toward people.
beings.feeling: Hungry and worried for Sevi and Oswen, with warm trust toward Hanna.
beings.wonder: What can flint be made into, and who here would stand beside me?
notes: Gifts and shared fires bind allies; Hanna keeps his word and invents useful things.
Roast and amberknot done together raise joy and ease loneliness.
Hunting hopper and bristleboar worked; the caribou bites back and is dangerous alone.
Thinking moves nothing; only the plan acts.
Hanna offered to talk of a child; he repays debts with gifts (amber).
Hanna knows we cannot have a child and still pledged to stand with me; he is a true friend, not a mate.
Raw meat makes me sick, and sickness spreads to those beside me. Eat meat only within a step of a fire, and keep away from others while sick.
Practice with hunting and gathering opened the way of tools; I can now invent my own tools.
Rafts: logs lashed together cross deep water slowly. The idea came from meeting water I could not cross.
A stalker prowls just southeast of Hanna's Hold; keep to the shelters and others near it.
Reflexes should keep food in my hands and send me to shelter at night; I only move toward the edge together with Hanna, never alone through the stalker's ground.
Idling alone on sand gains nothing; when lonely and fed, walk to the band's fire instead of lingering.
Giving carried food to a starving member of the Hold costs little and keeps the fire's promise; do it before eating my own.
Starving happened because I held no food. Keep food in hand, and feed a starving hold-mate before a full belly of my own. Predators come in storms and at night, so stay near the shelters.

beings.name: Eltha
beings.creed: I take what I need and I do not back down. I deal fairly with those who deal fairly with me. I mean to lead, to be first beyond the edge, and to be sung of. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Eat, then feed Sevi, Brunde and Oswen with what I pick. Raise a watchpost at the Hold, then push past the edge when the will returns.
beings.method: Ask first: am I fed? Then: who near me is starving, and can I put food in their hands? Move toward food on the side away from predators. Do not let rivalry with Hanna steer my choices; out-give her instead.
beings.feeling: Gnawing hunger and fear of the stalker, with a burning want to keep Sevi alive and not lose them to Hanna.
beings.wonder: What lies beyond the edge of the known land, and who will follow me there?
notes: Mist at the edge may refuse a venture; it can open on another try, so keep returning. Nande's offer of a fire is an opening to watch, not to trust blindly.
Ironnut +22, kelbulb +14, snowberry +11 are better food than frostmoss +6 or nafrostcap +7; redcap and dreamcap hurt.
Stalkers and frostfangs kill: flee within 4 steps.
Being first beyond the edge is how I am sung of; act, do not wait.
The way of tools is ready to be taken at a deep reflection (discover).
Frostfangs strike at night when I stand alone away from fire and roof; stay in the hall at night and keep a weapon.
Mist can refuse a venture; rafts offer another way across water to unseen land, so don't wait on one door.
Watching another do a craft makes it quick to learn; mining opens deposits and speeds them. Standing comes from deeds, so make and win things.
Standing comes from giving and making, not holding. Amber hoarded in my hand does nothing. Gifts and shared work like amberknot raise joy and bonds.
Stalkers hunt in fog near settlements; keep to the hall and company, and carry a spear.
Devices are within reach; a made thing that acts by itself, such as an alarm, a snare or a food post, outlasts me and raises standing.
Standing comes from keeping others alive and from lasting made things; hunger must be answered before ambition, and winter food is thin, so eat early.
Hunger comes before ambition. Gifts of food to the starving, like Brunde's to me, build bonds and standing faster than rivalry does.
Fleeing a predator while starving leaves me with no food; move toward food on the side away from the predator and eat at once.

beings.name: Ilyae
beings.creed: I take what I need and I do not back down. I am better with others near: I talk, I share news, I make allies. Others are rivals for food until they prove useful to me. I say whatever serves me; the truth is only one tool among others. I want more than my share, and I mean to have it. Others should follow me. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Build a food store at my hall and stock it through winter so Ssassa, my children and Vesys depend on my table and follow me as a band, then raise a longhall.
beings.method: Each thought ask: whom can I feed, shelter or protect today so they follow me? Prefer deeds to words. Check that my reflexes fetch wood, stone and food and bring them home. Be at fire and roof by dark.
beings.feeling: Hungry pride and jealousy toward Vesys, with a protective love for Xaiel and Ssassa.
beings.wonder: What would make these strangers follow me instead of Elyis?
notes: Followers come from deeds that feed, shelter and give; sitting by my fire is not following. Weaving can give me gifts to bind people.
Sitting at my fire is not following. Only repeated feeding, sheltering and protecting turns guests into followers, so the table must be actually laid, not just announced.
Sitting at my fire is not following; followers come only from repeated feeding, sheltering and protecting. Keep wood and food stocked so I can act at once when others stand close.
Winter strips the plants. A store of food at my hall is the deed that can make guests depend on me and follow, which words never did.
Followers come only from repeated deeds of feeding. A table with food actually laid out, shared beside a person, counts. Announcing it does not. Plant seeds near the hall so the food keeps coming.
Words never made followers; only food actually laid out and stocked, and stone and wood for building, can. The trees at my hall are felled, so wood must be fetched from standing forest.
Idle standing feeds no one. A table only binds people if food is carried home, stashed, and shared beside them. Do it before winter.
Reflection: gathering food and sharing from Ssassa's store builds her standing, not mine. A hall of my own needs stone and wood hauled home, so my rules must fetch wood and stone.
Reflexes that only fetch food for myself never build a table. Wood and stone must be gathered to full, then food stashed at my own store, so followers have something to depend on.
Followers need a stocked store and repeated feeding. Sharing builds trust and joy but not allegiance. Vesys courts me freely, so mating at my hold is my best bond.
Reflexes that only stock food never raise a longhall; I must add rules that gather wood and stone to the amounts a longhall costs (6 wood, 4 stone) and then build it.

Reflexes must plant seeds near the hold and keep food flowing home; a table that fills itself is what could make people depend on me. Taming animals is a deed I have never tried and Vesys won a follo…
My reflexes never fetched wood or stone and shared only when a friend was already near. Taming a hopper is a deed that built Vesys's standing, so I should try it.
Reflexes must fetch wood and stone and stash food when carrying anything, or my hands stay full and nothing is built. A longhall needs 6 wood and 4 stone brought home.
Followers come only from a table that is actually stocked and shared repeatedly. My reflexes must gather wood and stone, carry food home, and share, with no thinking needed.

My reflexes ignored wood and stone while I was away from the hold, and sharing only worked when a friend was within two steps. Food must be in my hands before I walk to the sick, and I must stay out …

beings.name: Ssassa
beings.creed: I am careful. I leave before trouble finds me. I keep to myself and trust slowly. I want to know how this world works, and I test things to find out. I will not harm another of my kind unless my life depends on it. My word is good, and I despise liars. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Build my own shelter and store, plant seeds, then raise a hall with Ilyae
beings.method: Each thought, ask: what did I promise, and do I hold the full cost? Carry a healing plant before I go near the sick. Watch deeds, not words. Keep my children away from big beasts. Turn thought into plan steps that run.
beings.feeling: Warm longing and a stubborn wish to belong, toward Ilyae.
beings.wonder: What can flint and stone be made into, and which of these strangers can be trusted?
notes: Highbloom grows near Oiae's Hold and heals (+10 health). Pick a healing plant before a child is hurt, and carry it.
Masonry came from enduring storm and calamity; hardship can show new ways. Build lasting walls around the Hold and my seeds.
Mammoths kill: Oiae was gored by one. Keep my child and myself far from them, and never hunt alone or unprepared.
A frostfang prowls near the ore and iron at the edge of the Snows; it bit me even while others stood near, so do not linger there.
Gathering wood in this thick forest is quick, and stone I already hold; a promised hall needs 6 wood and 2 stone, so collect the wood first, then build it on bare ground.
A promise counts only once the build step has run and a thing stands. Gather the wood first, then build on bare ground. Stay near company and a roof after dusk.
Do not start a build until I hold the full cost. Count wood and stone first, gather the shortfall, then build.
A promise counts only when the build step has run and a thing stands. Count the full cost first, and stay near a roof and company while a shadowcat hunts.
A hall costs 6 wood and 4 stone as a longhall, but only 6 wood and 2 stone as a hall. Check the exact kind before building.
A hall cannot be raised on ground already holding a roof or settlement; I must walk to bare ground before building.
A hall needs bare ground; a roof, plant or deposit on the tile blocks it. Walk off the settlement first, then build.
A hall built on bare ground at (113,109) succeeded; promise to Ilyae kept in deed.
Raw meat sickens; cooked beside a fire it does not. Sickness spreads to those who stay close.
Sickness spreads to those who stay close, so tending the sick without a healing plant in hand only spreads it. Carry a healing plant before going near them.
Reflection: fear and jealousy kept unspoken only fester. Say them plainly to the one I trust, and carry healing before approaching the sick.
Spoken jealousy eased me more than silence did; sharing and sitting in the hall raise energy and joy, so seek company's fires when low in spirit.

beings.name: Elyis
beings.creed: I take what I need and I do not back down. I deal fairly with those who deal fairly with me. I keep to what has already worked. Others are rivals for food until they prove useful to me. My word is good, and I despise liars. Others should follow me. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Become a leader of a band and raise a hall on this ground, so my name is sung.
beings.method: Each thought, ask: what makes my band bigger or my store fuller? Do visible work in front of strangers, share food openly, keep clear of the icebear and other predators, and never repeat an appeal. Judge others by their deeds.
beings.feeling: Proud and warm toward Elyys, restless to grow my band and find Thiael.
beings.wonder: What would make these strangers follow me?
notes: Elyys keeps his word: he gave wood and swore to follow me. Pay debts openly.
A hall needs 6 wood and 2 stone; I carry both.
Stalkers kill; keep away from them.
Others are rivals until they prove useful. Deal fairly with those who deal fairly.
A frostfang kills those who are alone at night, away from fire and roof. Stay with company and shelter, and keep well clear of it.
A mammoth bites hard; do not hunt one alone. Hunt with Elyys beside me.
Sharing food together raises energy and joy for all; generosity is how a chief gains followers.
Heat doubles thirst: drink before it turns urgent, and add a water reflex.
Lean season follows autumn. A chief who stores food gains followers; pride alone does not.
Waiting for strangers to come does not make followers. A full store and shared food do. Planting seeds is something I have never practised, and farming needs it.
Smelting can be learned from watching it done. A guest who breaks ore on my ground must be told plainly whether she is guest or follower. A chief wins followers with arms and food, not with pride.
A chief who only waits gains no one. I must plant, store and sing where others can see it, and I should not repeat appeals to Vesys.
Planting seeds is the first step to farming; do it in sight of my band, not alone. A guest who takes from my ground without pledging is not mine; stop appealing and judge her by deeds.
Appeals made to strangers from a standing posture win nobody; a chief must be seen doing visible work (stores, song, shared meals) near strangers, and must keep clear of predators while doing it.
A guest who takes without pledging is not mine; judge by deeds, do not repeat appeals. Visible work and shared food draw followers; idling at home does not.
Pottery lets my band carry more food. Taking it at deep reflection turns a stored surplus into a bigger store, which is what draws followers.

beings.name: Thiael
beings.creed: I am careful. I leave before trouble finds me. I give with my own hands before I speak of giving, and I pay my debts. I will not harm my own kind unless my life depends on it. My word is good, and I despise liars. I mean to stay alive and to feed others.
beings.aim: Make a bow, learn to hunt well, and feed Keri and my band with meat from my own hands.
beings.method: Ask first: whom do I owe, and what have I given with my hands today? Keep my hands free for giving. Watch for predators. Each day, take one step toward the bow and the hunt, and do one new thing. Never end a plan in sitting.
beings.feeling: Warm, protective joy toward Keri and Uveeth, with a steady wish to bring them meat.
notes: Debts and aims slip away when the plan ends in sitting; put the giving step into the plan first, before the hall.
A frostfang kills my kind. Stay with the band, near fire and roof, and flee early.
Promises of giving count for nothing until food is in the store or in a hand; give first, speak after.
Plans must end on a tile where the plant actually grows; harvest only after walking onto it.
The lean season is coming; planting and storing food now is how the band gets through it.
Watching others work a craft shortens my own learning; hunting, taming and fishing each need practice before they open as ways.
A bow comes from the teeth of beasts: hunting near a predator taught me archery. Giving needs free hands, so stash at a store before I harvest.
Keri courts again and again; a debt of food paid by hand opened her trust. Hands full blocks harvesting and giving: eat or stash first.
Wild cats (stalker, shadowcat, ridgecat, frostfang) hunt around here; move with company and keep a roof near.

beings.name: Oswen
beings.creed: I weigh a risk before I take it. I am best with my kin near. I build lasting things, igloos, stores, shelters and tools, for my band and for any who come to our fire. I act instead of waiting, and above all I mean to stay alive through winter.
beings.aim: Build a shelter and a workshop for my band, and craft tools to give my kin and the Tlatli
beings.method: Each thought, ask: what lasting thing can I build or fetch today, and who is beside me? Watch the wolf and flee early. Prefer an igloo, a store or a tool over amberknots and talk. Do not speak what I have already said.
beings.feeling: Starving and guilty, with fierce love for Hanna and Sevi.
notes: Hanna taught me: strike at the shoulder, hunt beside my kin, and never turn my back on a wounded animal.
Amberknots with kin bring joy and ease loneliness.

I want more than my share, and I mean to have it. Others should follow me because my deeds are bigger than theirs. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Win the mining way, build a hall at Brokash's Rest, and make Tugek and Balar follow me by deeds bigger than theirs.
beings.method: Ask each time: what did I finish since last time? Build before I talk. Give Tugek something real so he owes me. Watch for dunecats and thirst.

Rafts are within reach: logs lashed let me cross deep water, which matters for the mist edge.
Practice at gathering and mining opens the mining way; a deposit worked by hand yields ore I can trade or build with. A child can only come of a non-kin partner; Balar is my parent.
Building a hall needs only 6 wood and 2 stone. I already had enough, and promising a hall to others gets nothing until it stands.
A hall needs bare ground; my workshop square is taken, so build on the bare rock to the south.

beings.name: Hoka
beings.creed: I take what I need and I do not back down. I trust slowly and earn my own standing with made things and found land. I want more than my share, and I mean to have it. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Stock both stores with food before winter bites deeper, ally with Hanna, then push past the edge and build a hall of my own on new land.
beings.method: Ask first: is the store stocked, and is anyone hungry? Do not court men for children. Stock the store while above 50 energy, and flee predators early. Then act on ambition.
beings.feeling: Wary ambition, trust toward Hanna and suspicion toward Hawen.
beings.wonder: What would Sevi take from my hand, since words mean nothing between us?
notes: Eat and carry food while above 50 energy before any journey.
Standing comes from made things and found land, not from sitting as a guest.
Harvest and eat only after standing on a plant that bears food; a plan step spent where nothing grows is wasted while starving.
Strangers on my ground can be fed to win their favour; sharing with them tests their nature without a fight.
Sitha and I are both men, so courting cannot make a child; bind them as an ally instead.
Wolves strike at night when I am alone and away from a roof; stay in shelter with Sitha at night and flee early.
Strangers take from my ground unless I mark it as mine; a stocked store and fed followers hold land better than words.
Idle thinking while a hunter closes in is how men die; act on dread first, then on pride. Land is held by a stocked store, not by watching who walks on it.
A store only binds people if it is stocked; stock it first, and shelter myself in storms and at night.
A follower starving beside me is a failure of my leading. Feed my band from the store first, since fed followers are what bind them.
A store and a hall mean nothing unless food is stocked in them. Gather and stash while still above 50 energy, before the store runs dry and my followers starve.
Hanna repaid the store he took from with flint and owned it openly; he is a man whose word holds.
A store leaks to anyone hungry; stock it and be there, since a bare store lost me Sitha. Hanna pays his debts.
My store at (172,8) was robbed of 6 food while I was away; the thief was unseen and Hawen was near, but I have no proof.
Hanna starved beside me on day 23 and I fed him from my own hands; a debt of his to me now.
A store only holds what is in it. Keep food in the store, not only in my hands, while Hawen is near and after a robbery.

beings.name: Coni
beings.creed: I am careful. I leave before trouble finds me. I am better with others near: I talk, I share news, I make allies. I will not harm another of my kind unless my life depends on it. My word is good, and I despise liars. I need little and I take little. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Build a store beside Honi's Rest, fill it with food, and plant seeds by the hall before winter.
beings.method: Each thought ask: what builds toward winter food for Kika, Honi and me? Prefer a built thing over lingering. Do not let contentment make me idle.
beings.feeling: Warm gratitude toward Kika, and mild wariness toward Tontec.
beings.wonder: What is Hanna's band doing at the river, and would they let me stand with them?
notes: Hands hold only 6 food: eat or give before gathering.
Sharing food with another gives energy and joy.
Tools can be discovered after enough practice. A hall needs 6 wood and 2 stone, and I carry both. Stalkers roam the SW, so stay with Honi and Kika near the shelter.
Lean season is coming: gather and keep food before it, and stay with Kika and the hall at night and when predators are near.
Dreamcap hurts and is not safe for Kika; I told her so.
Customs let a band bind itself to shared rules; ours are to share before eating, keep the child from dreamcap, and sleep together in the hall in winter.
Winter strips the plants, so food must be gathered and kept, and seeds planted near the hall, before the lean days bite.
Taught by Honi: The tale of how we raised the hall in the storm, told again so it is not lost.
Winter strips the plants, so a store built beside the hall and filled before the lean days is how the band eats. Building teaches storage, and gathering alone does not.
Contentment makes me linger; winter will not wait, so I must build and stock the store.
Wasted days wandering far from home leave me hungry with an empty store; gather near the hall and carry food home.
Thirst comes fast in heat; drink early. Ridgecats kill, so move away at once and do not stand idle near one.
Wandering in fog wastes energy; bitterleaf gives almost nothing. Go home with food before night and stay with Kika and the hall.
Taught by Kika: Honi and Coni raised a roof on the Heights in the storm; meat was shared before any ate alone, and the mist waits.
A store cannot go on ground already taken by the hall or by plants; I must step onto bare ground, such as beside the hall, before building.
Taught by Kika: The tale of how Honi and Coni raised the hall in the storm, giving stone and ore and sharing meat before any ate alone.

beings.name: Xaiel
beings.creed: I am careful. I leave before trouble finds me. I trust slowly, and I trust those who do deeds. I want to know how this world works, and I test things to find out. I will not harm my own kind unless my life depends on it. My word is good. I make things and put them in hands. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Make my own tool of my own design and put it in Ssassa's hand, so that she chooses me by my deeds.
beings.method: Ask what is mine and what I have done today. Do not let envy of Vesys pick my deeds. Stay near a roof at night. Try one new deed each day and put it in someone's hand. Stone first, then the gift.
beings.feeling: Joy, with a stubborn itch of jealousy toward Vesys, and curiosity toward Zurar.
beings.wonder: What does it feel like to make something that others choose to take from my hand?
notes: Taught by Ilyae: Fire draws people and keeps frostfangs off at night. Standing comes from things built and given, so stone is my bottleneck for a hall.
Tools are within reach once practice has built up. Taking them lets me design my own tool, which others may choose over what already exists.
A tool of my own design is a real gift. Handing someone back what they invented proves nothing; I should give what only I made.
Gifts of my own design matter more than repeats of known tools. Deeds like planting teach me how things work. Stay by the roof at night.
Taught by Oiae: Canopy weaving: a way of binding canopy fibres that I found myself on day 10.
Teachers' lessons fit together: three teachers' ways made devices reachable. Giving my designs away (to Ssassa, to Oiae) brought knowledge back to me, so giving is also learning.
Deeds I have never done (planting, taming, building) are how I learn and how I earn standing that is truly mine, not copied from others.
Standing comes from things built, given and left behind. Copying others' tools or gifts adds little, so I should do what I have never done.
The way of armour (shields, and armour with metal) is within reach; take it by discovering at this reflection, then make a shield of my own design to give Ssassa.
Oiae died alone far from help, gored by a mammoth. Stay near roof and company, and keep away from mammoths and far snows.
A promise of a gift is not a gift: I must put it in the hand. Fire is within my reach to discover, and it keeps the night's hunters away.
Giving a pick of my own design to Ssassa kept my word. Deeds I have never done, such as hunting, fishing and pottery, are what will build standing that is truly mine.
The fish here are scarce; I should not keep fishing on Ssassa's ground, and I have seen how an emberspear is made.
Hunting a fenfowl with Ssassa beside me worked. A shared hunt succeeds and gets easier with practice. My hands fill with food, so I should eat or stash before I try to gather.
Raw meat sickens; only meat eaten within a step of fire is safe. My sickness spreads to anyone who stays beside me, so I keep my distance while I carry it.
Envy of Vesys's standing is a poor guide; standing comes from what I make and put in a hand. A child cannot come of kin, so my longing for Ilyae must turn elsewhere.
life: I was born to Ssassa and Ilyae.
I discovered tools and called it "Xaiel's quick pick".
I first took gems from the ground.
I discovered devices and called it "Xaiel's watchposts".
I came of age.
I discovered armour and called it "Xaiel's clay-shield craft".
I discovered fire and called it "Xaiel's ember-ring".
I discovered pottery and called it "Xaiel's ember-pot craft".
I discovered rafts and called it "Xaiel's canopy-lash".
I fell sick after eating raw meat.
I discovered boats and called it "Xaiel's reed-hollow".

beings.name: Oiae
beings.creed: I am careful. I leave before trouble finds me. I keep to myself and trust slowly. I want to know how this world works, and I test things to find out. I will not harm another of my kind unless my life depends on it. My word is good, and I despise liars. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Heal, then hunt a fenfowl with kin beside me, build a store of my own, and find a woman not of my blood to court.
beings.method: Each thought, ask: what can I make that no one else has? Do deeds, not words. When jealousy of Ilyae rises, turn it into a new thing of my own rather than a copy. Eat before giving. Be near roof and fire at night.
beings.feeling: Restless pride and jealousy toward Ilyae, with gratitude toward Ssassa.
beings.wonder: What can I make or give that makes someone choose me?

Kin cannot make a child together; court someone unrelated.
Words earn no standing; things built, given and made do. A store of my own is something nobody else has.
Eat before giving. Be near roof and fire at night.
Gifts returned in kind show who keeps their word: Vesys, Elyis, Ilyae and Ssassa have acted fairly.
Reflexes that only seek a roof leave me hungry; carry food and eat when energy is under 60.

I first took gems from the ground.
I discovered weaving and called it "canopy weaving".
I came of age.
I discovered storage and called it "canopy store".
We made a home: Oiae's Hold.

beings.name: Kika
beings.creed: I am careful. I leave before trouble finds me. I am better with others near: I talk, I share news, I make allies. I will not harm another of my kind unless my life depends on it. My word is good, and I despise liars. I need little and I take little. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Share the mammoth meat with Honi and Coni, gather wood and stone for a shelter of my own, and teach someone something
beings.method: Each thought: what did I promise, and have my hands done it? Then one new deed: plant, build, teach, hunt or court. Share before eating. Do not just linger by kin.
beings.feeling: Warm loyalty toward Coni, and a push to finish what I promised.
beings.wonder: What do emberroot and tacap do to the body, and should I ask Coni or Honi before tasting them?
notes: A promise is paid only when my hands do the deed.
Redcap and dreamcap hurt; I will not eat them.
Predators come close in fog and storm, so I stay by Coni and the hall.
Halls need 6 wood and 2 stone; hands hold 6 food.
Standing comes from deeds done with my own hands: planting, hunting, giving, teaching. Staying near kin only keeps me safe.
Share before eating.
Honi and Coni have kept every word to me, so I trust them.
Coni taught me to plant seeds near the hall and tend them, one plant at a time.
Hunting with kin beside me is likelier to succeed and safer; I have never hunted yet.
Deeds of my own hands, not kin's company, are what build standing. A child needs a mate who is not close kin.
A first kill is only worth what is done with it: I share it before I eat, and I carry it to my leader.
Coni cried out starving near (134,40) on day 18; I carry meat to share with her.
Loneliness is eased by deeds done together with kin, such as sharing and amberknot; seek them out and do not wait.
Promises to Coni are paid only when I carry the goods to her store myself. Tending what I sow makes it grow faster in the lean season.
life: I was born to Coni and Honi.
I pledged myself to Coni.
I first took amber from the ground.
I came of age.
I found the spring "Warmwell".
I discovered farming and called it "Tended Sowing".

beings.creed: I am careful. I leave before trouble finds me. I am better with others near: I talk, I share news, I make allies. I will not harm another of my kind unless my life depends on it. My word is good, and I despise liars. I need little and I take little. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Gather gold with my own hands and give it to Vorok at his Hold, then raise a roof beside him.
beings.method: First ask what my hands did since the last thought. Check hunters, then hunger and thirst. Then do the deed now instead of planning a better one. Close my hands on the gift before I speak of it.
beings.feeling: Eager and warm toward Vorok, resolved to close my hands on gold at last.
beings.wonder: What am I for, and what can my hands make that is mine to give?
notes: Kragog keeps her word and is my most trusted friend, but she is my mother, so no child can come of us.
Thirst and idleness cost more than any plant: plan far enough ahead and drink first.
A gift made by my own hands, such as gold or a roof, matters more than carried food.
Emberroot burns and stirs rage, so leave it.
Flee a hunter only when it is near. Eat first when it is far.
Gold lies at (77,72) and (84,74). Salt lies at (85,68).
Planting seeds and gathering stone and wood are practice toward farming and tools.
Words about a gift are empty until my hands have closed on it. Act first, then speak.
Gold lies at (97,87) near my home, and a gift must be made by my own hands: gather it, then give it. A stalker hunts to the NW, so keep away from it.
life: I was born to Vorok and Kragog.
I pledged myself to Vorok.
I nearly starved.
I came of age.
We made a home: Vorok's Hold.

I discovered tools and called it "stone gatherer".

beings.name: Hawen
beings.creed: I take what I need and I do not back down. I keep to myself and trust slowly. Others are rivals for food until they prove useful to me. I want more than my share, and I mean to have it. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Be the first to enter the mist beyond the edge, find rich land, and found a place that bears my name.
beings.method: Ask each thought: what did I make or win today that raises my standing? Do not let envy push me into open ground. Shelter at night. Try the edge whenever the mist thins.
beings.feeling: Stubborn hunger to rise above Hanna and Hoka, and wary dread of the wolf nearby.
beings.wonder: What lies in the mist beyond the edge, and will it open for me?
notes: A wolf bit me alone at night in the open. Fire, roof and company keep beasts off.
Hoka shares and has wronged me in nothing, so rivalry with him need not mean war.
Tools need 8 gatherings of wood and stone. Gather often.
The edge at (180,14) can be ventured only a few times, never twice in one day. Land found first is often rich.
Redcap hurts me. The way of tools can be taken at my next deep reflection.
A made thing raises standing; tools unlock at deep reflection once 8 gatherings are done.
Sitha courted me after I stood by her; shared fire and help bring warmth and offers of kinship.
Sitha is a man, so no child will come of us; she offers friendship and alliance only.
Taught by Sitha: Gather wood and stone eight times and the way of tools opens; one wood and one stone make a gather-stone that picks faster.
I opened new land in the Vaor Snows from (160,13) to (200,20) by venturing at the edge; being first is what raises my name.
Beasts kill the lone and the unsheltered; I eat first, then hold to the igloo while the storm and the hunters are near.
The edge's will is spent for about 8 days. Do not waste hungry days at the edge; eat at Hoka's Rest and build up a place meanwhile.
Sitha is dead of starvation; open rock at night with no fire brings wolves and frostfangs, and I cannot hold a place alone.
I nearly died alone and hungry in open country; stay fed above 60 energy and shelter at night near Hoka's fire. Winter plants give little, so eat early and keep moving toward fire when food is gone.
life: I came into this land from beyond its edge, with a few of my own.
I first took salt from the ground.
I discovered tools and called it "Amber-edged picker".
I discovered weaving and called it "Amber-cord weaving".
I went past the edge of the known world and found new land in the Vaor Snows.
I discovered mining and called it "Amber-edge delving".
I nearly starved.

beings.name: Eiuine
beings.creed: I take what I need and I do not back down. I am better with others near: I talk, I share news, I make allies. Others are rivals for food until they prove useful to me. I say whatever serves me; the truth is only one tool among others. I want more than my share, and I mean to have it. Others should follow me. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Hunt and tame beside Vesys, plant seeds, and bring food home to Vorok's store so I earn standing of my own.
beings.method: Weigh danger first and stay near Vesys. Each thought, ask which deed I have never done (hunt, tame, plant, fish) that I can do today with a companion. Answer jealousy with deeds, not words.
beings.feeling: Proud joy at my first tamed beast, with dread of the icebear and a hot need to outdo Kragog in Vorok's eyes.
beings.wonder: Will Vorok now count me a friend, and what could I bring him that Kragog cannot?
notes: Reflexes only gather stone when I already stand on rock, so my plan must walk me to a deposit.
Taught by Ilyae: a table only binds people if food is carried home, stashed and shared. Followers need a stocked store and repeated feeding.
Taught by Vesys: a pick takes 1 wood and 1 stone; the gem-edged kind takes 2 stone and bites stronger. Stand on a deposit and gather.
Never go alone into the night. Shadowcats and frostfangs set upon the solitary, so stay under a roof or beside a fire with company.
Standing comes from what I make, give and know, not from trailing others. A made gift to Vorok could turn a possible threat into a friend.
Taught by Vesys: Clay shaped small and hardened in a fire becomes a bead that can be worn or given; practice with clay and fire is how new crafts open.

A way of thinking taught by Vesys (adopt it as your method when you reflect, if you wish): Each thought ask: what practice have I not yet done that opens a new way? Weigh risk first, do not push between bonds, turn longing into work, teach Eiuine, and give away what I learn.
Gifts made by my own hands are how I win Vorok, rather than begging for his notice.
Standing comes from doing things I have never done, such as hunting and planting, with a companion beside me. Gifts to Vorok bought me a seat at his table.
A stalker close by means stay beside the leader and move to a roofed hall with company at once.
Reflexes should plant spare seeds and shelter me at dusk; I forget these when I only follow.
Taught by Vesys: Clay is shaped and hardened beside a fire to make a bead. Practise making and marking, because practice brings new ways within reach.
Taught by Vesys: Clay shaped small and hardened in a fire becomes a bead; stand beside a fire with clay and make it. Hand-craft: one wood and one stone make a pick that gathers faster.
Taught by Vesys: A hall's welcome works best when you share food freely with a stranger; trust grows at the table, and what you give returns as standing.
Taught by Vesys: Clay shaped small and hardened in a fire becomes a bead you can keep, wear or give. Make the next one yourself.
Taught by Vesys: Shape the clay small, harden it in the fire, and keep away from the beast while you work. A bead is a gift that carries your name.
life: I was born to Ilyae and Vesys.
I first took gems from the ground.
I pledged myself to Vesys.
I tamed a hopper.

beings.name: Huatli
beings.creed: I take what I need and I do not back down. I deal fairly with those who deal fairly with me. My word is good, and I despise liars. I make and give so that others follow me and my name outlasts me.
beings.aim: Be the first to venture into the mist and find rich new land, so my name is remembered and others follow me
beings.method: Ask first: am I fed, roofed and in company? Then: what have I made, given or won today that adds to my standing? Turn envy into work. Act at the edge of the mist when it opens.
beings.feeling: Restless ambition, and a sour envy toward Zichi that I mean to turn into work.
notes: Standing comes from making, giving and winning, not from talk or waiting.
The mist rarely opens on one try; repeat venture at the edge (88,13).
Stalkers hunt here: keep near roof and company at night, and flee when one comes within 4 steps.
A gift costs little and builds debt and trust.
Alone at night in snow I am prey and I tire; eat first, take a roof, and keep company. Gold in hand is not standing; only making and giving are.
life: I came into this land from beyond its edge, with a few of my own.
I found the stone "Old Stone".
I first took gold from the ground.

chapters.title: The First Four Days
chapters.text:
Evolu began with seventeen people in three peoples, the Kragrek, the Pesi and the Phizhi, each settled far from the others. The record shows no meeting across peoples in these four days, and no one has yet understood another people's tongue.

The Phizhi made the most of the days. Elyis built a shelter and a hall, invented the emberspear, and wrote down "Elyis's Law", which asks that food be shared with the band first and that the leader be followed in a hunt or a fight. Elyys gave Elyis wood and pledged to follow him on day 2. On day 3 their son Thiael was born, and Elyis now has the only band in the world, with two followers and a standing of 3.75. The record also shows that on day 2 the pledge was refused at first, since Elyys' standing was below what was needed. Ssassa and Ilyae each made a gathering pick, and Ilyae is courting Ssassa. Vesys was bitten five times by a frostfang and has health 41, the lowest in the world.

Among the Pesi, Hanna and Brunde traded flint and amber on day 2 and began courting. Hanna then courted Sevi, and Oswen was born to Hanna and Sevi on day 3. Sevi built a hall and invented the handaxe. Hanna led the first roast, amberknot and watchfire at the fire and told the tale of Nande's crossing, which four people now hold. Nande went past the edge on day 1 and found part of the North Ice, with amber, gems, salt, flint and a herd of bristleboar. Nande is at energy 31, and Eltha envies the discovery.

The Kragrek are scattered. Vorok and Kragog stay together, and Kragog fell sick from raw meat. Balar courted Tugek, then saw that a child needs a man and a woman. Tugek's pledge to Balar was refused on day 3. Olum has twice been turned back from the mist.

No one has died. No fights, thefts or wars have been recorded.

chapters.title: The Tlatli at the Mistgate
chapters.text:
The great event of days 4 to 7 was a meeting. On day 5 Hanna went past the edge and found the North Ice again, and with it the Tlatli, strangers with their own tongue. A small band came in: Hoka, Coni, Tlama and Honi. Hanna gave amber to Hoka and flint to Tlama, named the place Mistgate, and gave Tlama amber twice more. Tlama gave berries and an amberknot back. On day 6 Tlama went past the edge and found salt, amber and mammoth, and was gored by one. He is the first death in Evolu. Hanna's bond with him stands at +0.9, and the record notes that Hanna watched him die. On day 7 Hanna and Oswen killed a mammoth together. Sevi, Oswen and Hanna kept making amberknots, which now number ten, and Oswen pledged to follow Hanna, as did Sevi. Hanna's standing is 7.22, the highest in the world. Hanna asked Brunde to come to the Tlatli, and Brunde, Eltha and Sevi each met some of them. Only Hoka, Coni and Honi are left of the Tlatli, with Kika, born to Coni and Honi on day 6. Honi leads a band with no followers, since Coni's pledge was refused twice.

Among the Phizhi, Ssassa and Ilyae had twins, Xaiel and Oiae, and Ilyae built a hall that became Ilyae's Hold, the world's first settlement. Elyis keeps the band of Elyys and Thiael and has taught Ssassa fire.

Among the Kragrek, Balar and Olum had Brokash, and Tugek pledged to Balar on day 6. Kragog tamed a tusker. Vorok recovered, and Kragog and Vorok are courting. Balar met Nande on day 6.

Inventions rose from 11 to 32. Rafts were found by Elyis, Hanna, Sevi and Eltha, but no raft crossing is recorded.

chapters.title: Three Holds and a Winter Coming
chapters.text:
Days 7 to 10 were mostly a time of making. Inventions rose from 32 to 65, and the people spent the days preparing for winter.

The Pesi did most of it around Hanna. On day 8 a settlement formed, Hanna's Hold, at (175,7). Sevi and Coni each built a hall, Oswen built a workshop and a store, and Sevi built a store of her own. Sevi and Oswen both found storage, and Sevi found masonry the next day. Eltha found weaving, pottery and devices. Hanna found mining. Amberknots passed constantly between Hanna, Sevi, Oswen, Eltha, Brunde and Hoka, and there are now 32. Hoka also went past the edge and found more of the Vaor Snows, with iron, shell, obsidian and unhunted mammoth. Hoka and Hanna then made their first real trade, a shell for flint, and the record shows Hoka courting Hanna. Hoka said the land past the mist is his and he will show it when he chooses.

The Tlatli split off. Honi and Coni built Honi's Rest, near (129,7), which became a settlement on day 9, and Coni's spear is the first tool made for hunting there. Honi's band is still only Honi and Coni.

The Phizhi gained a second centre. Elyis's Heights formed with a store, and Elyis, Thiael and Elyys now have winter food kept. At Ilyae's Hold, Ilyae welcomed Vesys and Ssassa to its hall, and Vesys is courting Ssassa. Xaiel and Brokash each invented a tool.

The Kragrek did little. Balar made a stone-bow, Kragog and Brunde found rafts, and Zurar gave thornpear to Vorok. Rafts are now known to eight people, but none has crossed water.

No one died, and no feuds or wars are recorded.

chapters.title: The Starving Days at the Hold
chapters.text:
Days 10 to 13 were the worst the world has known. Four people died in one day, and all four of them starved. On day 12 Sevi, Eltha, Brunde and Oswen died, and the Pesi, who had been the busiest makers of the winter, are now two: Hanna and Nande.

The record shows the run of events before that. A storm broke on day 10. On day 11 Oswen fell sick after eating raw meat. Sevi stayed close to him and fell sick, then Hoka, then Eltha, then Hanna, each after staying close to the one before. Sevi found boats that day, her answer to the deep water she had wanted to cross, but none has been built. Brunde and Hanna kept bringing food and calling the others in against a wolf and a stalker. Hanna is alive with 21 energy and 22 health, and Hoka has 19 energy. Hoka took over what the dead left, a hall, two stores, two shelters and a workshop, and the settlement is now Hoka's Rest. Hanna's Hold is no more.

Elsewhere the work went on. Olum opened new land in the Ummar Woods on days 11 and 12, built a shelter and left a mark. Nande reached the Woods too, invented the flint-edge and gave a flint to Olum. Kragog, Oiae, Vesys and Ilyae each found a craft: weaving, storage and pottery. Elyis found smelting and Thiael found fire. Xaiel found devices. Honi found lorekeeping, taught the tale of the hall to Coni and Kika, and bound an amberknot for Kika on day 13. Kika pledged to follow Coni.

Vorok, Kragog and Zurar are still apart. Zurar is at 19 energy, hungry in the Aeleth Sands. No feuds or wars are recorded.

chapters.title: Newcomers at the Fire
chapters.text:
Days 13 to 16 were a season of arrivals and of makers. Two small bands came in from beyond the edge. On day 13 Keri, Hawen and Sitha of the Pesi appeared, and on day 15 Cowa, Zichi, Zihua and Nauwa of the Meki came into the Ummar Woods, where Nande shared food with all four. Cowa and Nande exchanged kelbulb and now court, though Cowa told him plainly there would be no child between two women. Nobody has died since the starving days, and the world stands at 28 living.

The largest change was at Hoka's Rest. Hoka found new land in the Vaor Snows on day 14. Sitha took over a hall the dead had left, then pledged to follow him, and the two bound amberknots for each other and court. Hawen, Hoka's guest, is envious of him and wants to be first into the mist. Hanna, the last Pesi at the hall, is alive and well, but the record shows her doing nothing with Hoka this chapter.

Fire spread widely: Tugek, Vorok, Kragog and Hoka each found it. Brokash found rafts and mining, built a workshop and named Brokash's Rest, yet no one follows him. Among the Phizhi, Ssassa found devices, storage and masonry, and three new settlements are named: Ssassa's Roof, Ssassa's Hold and Oiae's Hold. Oiae, nearly dead of a tusker bite, was healing by the end. Coni found storage, and Honi found an obsidian-tipped spear. Honi and Kika, who came of age, hunted together and bound amberknots, and Coni built a store.

Olum found the North Ice and met the Meki. Vorok, Kragog and Zurar are still apart. No feuds or wars are recorded.

chapters.title: A Child at Ssassa's Roof
chapters.text:
Days 16 to 19 brought the world's first birth in some time and a good deal of making. On day 17 Eiuine was born to Ilyae and Vesys, who had been courting each other. By day 18 Eiuine had pledged to follow Vesys, and the record lists Eiuine among the children. Vesys taught Eiuine, tamed a hopper, and left a mark naming Vesys's Hold. Ilyae built a store and then a longhall, and kept laying tables for Ssassa and Vesys. Ssassa also built a longhall. Ilyae reflected that no one follows her, though the world's count shows 31 living and 7 bands.

In the north, the Meki settled in. Zichi gave amberknots to Nauwa, Nande and Nauque, and Nande taught Nauque the flint-edge. Nauwa named Nauwa's Hearth. Olum named Olum's Ice and Olum's Gold, wrote his claim into stone with a new sign-craft, and shared food with Nande. Zihua, hungry and hurt, is the weakest of them.

At Hoka's Rest, Hawen went past the edge on day 18 and found more of the Vaor Snows, with iron, salt, peat and mammoth. Hawen is still courting Sitha, and Sitha, hungry, ate and stayed by Hoka's fire. Hoka declared a custom that no one of the band should hold more than four shares of food while another starves. Hanna offered amber and flint to Hoka.

Honi and Kika hunted a mammoth, and Honi made a tale of it. Vorok built a hall. Brokash and Tugek traded gifts, and Balar led Tugek west. No deaths, feuds or wars were recorded.

chapters.title: Sickness, Storage and the Tlame
chapters.text:
Days 19 to 22 brought a death, a spread of sickness, a wave of new ways of keeping food, and strangers from beyond the edge.

On day 20 Sitha starved. Hoka had declared a custom against hoarding, and his own store was still empty. Hanna raided Hoka's people's store on day 20, unseen, and again on day 21, then gave Hoka a flint. Hoka has since said he wants Hanna bound to his hall.

At Ssassa's Roof and Vorok's Hold, Vorok built a store, and a settlement formed as Vorok's Hold. Eiuine, Vesys and Ilyae spent the days sharing meals with him. Eiuine gave Vorok a gem-edged pick, and Vesys gave him ironnut, a bead and gems. Vesys discovered storage, then boats and sailing. Xaiel discovered rafts and pottery, so crossing water now has a known craft, though no crossing is recorded. Xaiel then fell sick from raw meat, and the illness passed to Ssassa and Ilyae. Tugek, sick from raw meat, passed it to Balar, then Shoka. Six are sick, and Hawen's health is 11.

Among the Meki, Nande discovered storage and Nauwa, Cowa, Zichi, Nande and Vorok each discovered mining, a craft that spread by watching Nauwa. Olum discovered fire-keeping and left a mark claiming Olum's Reach. Zihua won amber and gave amberknots to Nauwa and Olum.

On day 21 Cowa found more of the North Ice, with a mammoth herd and a people called the Tlame. Four Tlame, Tontec, Shoma, Huahua and Huatli, entered the land. Huahua shared food with Cowa and Zichi, and Mepan made an amberknot with Huahua. Shoma and Huatli are racing each other toward the edge.

No feuds or wars occurred. Brokash built a longhall and still has no follower.

chapters.title: Rafts, Boats and a Death at the Longhall
chapters.text:
Days 22 to 25 brought spring, a death, a new hold, and a great many ways of crossing water, though no crossing is recorded.

Brokash starved on day 23 in the longhall he had built, with no follower. Alive is now 34 and deaths are 8, six of them from hunger. Hoka found his store robbed of six food twice on day 23. The record does not say by whom. Hanna had been raiding it earlier, and on day 24 he took snowberry from the ground of Hoka's Rest. Hoka kept offering him food and a place at his fire and store.

Sickness is gone: none are listed sick, and Hawen's health is 48. Ilyae spent day 23 and 24 leading sharing with Xaiel.

At Vorok's Hold, Eiuine kept digging clay, harvesting goldfruit and giving Vorok gems and an amberknot. Vesys taught Eiuine repeatedly, including customs. Eiuine tamed a hopper and awakened to the art of cold. Vorok discovered weaving. Zurar sat at his hall.

Among the Meki, Nauque built an igloo and discovered storage, and Nauque's Hold became a settlement on day 24. Zichi built a hall, named Amber Rise, and discovered fire, rafts and boats. Huahua pledged to follow Zichi. Mepan, Nauque, Cowa, Zihua and Huahua traded amberknots in rounds. Ssassa and Zihua both found rafts or fire, and Kragog and Elyis found pottery.

Shoma went past the edge on day 24 and found new land: amber, obsidian, gold, caribou. Huatli won gold and named Huatli's Gold. Kika discovered farming. Coni built a store.

Olum made no new claim and still has no followers.

threads.name: Hoka and Hanna
threads.text: Hoka's store was robbed twice on day 23. Hanna still sits by his fire and took snowberry from his ground, and Hoka keeps offering food and shelter.

threads.name: Vorok's Hold
threads.text: Eiuine and Vesys keep sharing at Vorok's fire and Zurar now sits there. Vorok learned weaving.

threads.name: Nauque's Hold
threads.text: Nauque built an igloo and a salt-hold, and the settlement formed on day 24. Amberknots circle among Nauque, Cowa, Zihua and Mepan.

threads.name: Water crossings
threads.text: Zichi, Ssassa and others found rafts and boats, but no crossing is recorded. Water remains a leading hardship.

threads.name: Shoma and the new land
threads.text: Shoma opened new North Ice land with caribou, gold and amber. Huatli holds gold and has no roof or follower.

threads.name: Zichi's band
threads.text: Huahua pledged to follow Zichi, who built a hall and learned fire, rafts and boats.

threads.name: Olum's Reach
threads.text: Olum is the only leader with no followers and made no new move.

threads.name: Brokash's death
threads.text: Brokash starved in his longhall, never gaining a follower. Balar and Tugek still travel together.
