ideas.text: [NOW: built, to be watched and tuned] standing: earned by wealth, deeds, knowledge, children, works, followers, giving and renown, lost through shame; needed before anyone will follow; special things add to it
[NOW] songs, poems and tales about people and about how the world came to be: kept, told aloud, changing a little in each mouth; bards who carry them
[NOW] a community learning from what befalls its own: a death and how it came, a sickness and its cause, a thing that worked
[NOW] everything that is used wears and regrows by what is around it: pasture, forest, deposits; great deposits that last
[NOW] bridges; weapons for one hand and for a siege (bow, shield, armour, ram, catapult, guns); defence
[NOW] the old workings of the world weakening as the ages of knowledge advance

[NOW] the known world ends in mist and can be pushed back: one who stands at the edge can venture in, and a wide strip of new land may open, continuing the rivers, shores and kinds of ground it joins, with rich deposits and a herd; a band has three tries and then must wait, and once any strip has opened the mist parts for no one for a day, so that the known world grows slowly (laws explore.*, among them gapDays)

[NOW] the world is a globe: east joins west, and it ends at two poles of ice that are different countries (white bears, wolves, caribou and mammoths in the north; penguins, seals and stormbirds in the south; whales and orcas in both seas). Between them lie three climates: the ice, cold all year; the lands with seasons; and a warm belt of rainforest and desert with no winter. Each kind of country has its own plants, animals and people, and both people and animals are drawn back to their own (law drives.homeland)
[NOW] the dog, easily won with food, which stands with its keeper in the hunt and draws a sled over snow; the igloo, raised on snow from nothing; the canoe and the kayak
[NEXT] rain and flood as the weather of the warm belt; a day that goes round the world

[NOW] women and men: a child comes of one of each; twins are a girl and a boy; children come sooner when both parents are well fed and well (mate.plentyCooldown); a grown body can swim narrow water; plants grow faster in spring, rain and at harvest; animals breed by season and by their numbers, and herds return from the rim when few (ecology.grazerTarget, ecology.herdReturn); deposits refill slowly (ecology.lodeRegrow)

[NOW] peoples that last: newcomers who come into the land when the living are few (law arrivals.*, event newcomers), twins (mate.twinChance), longer lives, a milder lean season; what the dead built stands empty and can be claimed by anyone, to begin a home or add to a band's; elders moved to hand on what only they know

[NOW] necessity as the mother of invention: what beings suffer (hunger, the lean season, cold, thirst, sickness, beasts, deaths, water they cannot cross, strife, storm, strange speech) sharpens them toward the ways that answer it; knowing neighbouring ways helps; you can set which hardships spur which way (op spur) and how strongly need counts (laws discovery.*)

[NOW] culture as something that can be read and followed: every tale, song, poem, myth, teaching, saying, lesson and way is an idea with an origin, holders and a path of spread; teachings that can be begun, heard, taken up and given up; talismans and carved figures; your statistics show which ideas are held most and which have crossed between peoples

[NEXT] objects of culture with real benefits and trade value beyond the first talismans and carvings: special gems, named relics that gather a history; secret manuscripts holding spells, knowledge or cures

[NEXT] religious figures, sages with followers, cults, schools of thought and religions that form and compete, some of the light and some of the dark; benefits, secrets, abilities and costs for those who belong, in some cases sacrifice; shrines, temples and churches that members pay toward
[NEXT] tribute and taxes for the common good: stores, works, defence; guilds and secret societies that give benefit and take dues
[NEXT] schools for children and the young, later universities: skills learned faster than alone
[NEXT] trade between lands and across water; ports; colonies as a named act; diplomats, spies, saboteurs; alliances open and secret
[NEXT] kinds of rule: councils and votes, shared holding, private holding, rule by the armed

[NOW] what is not forgotten: a blow or a theft that is seen leaves a grudge that holds a bond down until three gifts mend it or long time passes; a gift in need leaves a kindness that holds it up (laws culture.grudgeDays, kindDays, mendGifts); hunting together (fight.packBonus) and skill that grows with each hunt; telling by a fire, which makes tales; a roof that brings children sooner (mate.roofCooldown)

[NEXT] grudges from defeat or a stolen mate; compensation greater than gifts; peacemakers and peace ceremonies; hard feelings rarer inside a family or band than across them, and arising from conflict, wealth, history or charisma
[NEXT] rivalry for mates; heroes whose deeds spread as lore, to whom tribute is paid and whom the ambitious challenge; duels in which the winner takes most of what the loser holds
[NEXT] fighting, hunting and defending together as learned skills; calling for help and answering it
[NEXT] talents: skill in a way drawing one on along its line; learning what a way demands through dreams, visions from herbs or a shaman's prophecy, and quests to gather what it needs
[NEXT] bandits in new lands; stranger settlements friendly or hostile, with things to trade; farms and flocks as a settlement's steady food
[LATER] monsters that wander in rarely and can be killed only by a band together; their capture, taming and breeding from guarded eggs that others will try to steal
[NEXT] later callings that come with standing and ways: alchemists, scholars, scientists
[LATER: ages three and four] siege warfare and defensive works; weapons of war that are carried to a siege
[LATER] what is built must be kept up or it decays; taking down old buildings to raise new ones; concrete and metal as building stuffs carried from where they are won

[LATER] crowding brings troubles; religion, care for the poor, clean water, public works, places for play, music, dance and art, and the handling of waste ease them; places of buying and selling; healers, pharmacies, hospitals
[LATER] places of invention that quicken discovery; revolutions in knowledge that give great advantage to those who take them up, while others hold out or follow
[LATER] the sciences as knowledge in their own right, in generations: biology, chemistry, physics, then the second and third of each

[FAR: ages five and six] sources of power in order: coal, oil and gas, falling water, wind, the atom, the sun, fusion, the ground of things; each needing what must be found: oil fields, uranium, copper, silicon, rare earths, carbon, diamond
[FAR] speech at a distance in order: marks, smoke, birds, radio, telephone, the joined machines, the machine in the hand; reckoning machines need factories to make them
[FAR] machines that fly: balloons, propellers, jets, for carrying and for war; land vehicles for war

[FAR] the buildings of a great city: dwellings for many, high towers, offices, halls of rule, guards and fire-watch, water and power works and the lines that carry power, barracks and camps of war, markets, harbours, airfields, stations, factories, plants that remake waste
[FAR] new materials far down the tree: plastics, silicon, rare earths
[FAR] the knowledge of what makes a body: changing animals and oneself
[FAR] weapons beyond guns

[LAST] a spaceport: ships that come and go, goods and strange devices from other worlds, visitors who need their own air and live beside the port; their devices do what nothing else does (power, food, healing, terrible weapons, things not understood) and are worth much for being rare
tribal bonds and family bonds, and the pull between them; mating within a people versus between peoples
more kinds of animals at several levels of predator and prey; riding and working animals
many herbs and plants that heal, harm, change attributes or behaviour; plants that open the mind
spirits of places, good and ill, rarely found; mythical animals, monsters and places that help or harm
shamans who heal or affect crops, weather, animals and people; celebrations and ceremonies; crime and punishment; secret knowledge and shared knowledge
professions and castes; salt, caves, mills and kilns; sieges; promises and debts; rituals with force
a world rich to look at and to hear, that changes as it ages
Places of power as anchors that people compete over and settle around; a contested place between two camps could create contact that scarcity alone never did.
Death should leave a trace: the place where someone fell could become a site that touches visitors with grief or lore, a seed for ancestor belief.
Leaders without followers are a lasting tension. Give them acts that cost something and visibly benefit others, rather than handing out followers.
Beads, charms and wards are seeds for currency and status: if they circulate, a later recipe could require them.
Watch whether noticed thefts or takings from settled ground lead to a custom against taking, which would be the first law born from a crime.
Fear of predators is the strongest shared feeling. A leader who can visibly lessen it for others may be the natural route to the first band of three or more.
First contact between peoples who cannot understand each other: watch whether gifts come before words, and whether a made thing given across peoples opens trade.
Each land holds what the others lack. A recipe or a way that needs a thing from another people's land would make crossing worthwhile.
The sea divides the world. Whoever first makes a raft meets a people that has never seen them.
Children change every drive. If a first birth comes, watch whether the family drive pulls people toward one camp.
A resource held by one people and wanted by another (salt for keeping meat, shell for stringing, wool for cloaks) is the natural seed of trade: watch which crosses first.
A woolly grazer is the link between weaving and herding: watch whether the first taming comes from weavers or from hunters who spare an animal.
Care for the sick and hungry may be the real road across the wall of language, and those who give across it the first translators.
A recipe that wears a tool might pull tools out of the hand and into the field.

A song at the fire may be the first shared culture. If nightsong or telling becomes a habit in one band, a singer could carry it to another camp, and a song of the band could become part of who they are.
Graves as shared ground: if a resting place is visited by two peoples, shared grief may become the first ground both hold sacred, and a seed for ancestor rites.
A hardy food that persists in winter is a fallback, not a store. Watch whether people remember where it grows and return when the cold comes: the first knowledge of place tied to a season.

Raw-meat sickness as a teacher: a people that falls sick from raw flesh and then finds fire could keep a saying that cooked meat is safe. This would be the first lesson a community learns from its own suffering, and worth watching among the Kragrek.
Gifts without trades: 48 gifts and 0 trades so far. Watch whether a true exchange ever appears, or whether gift-giving itself becomes the economy, with amberknots as the first token.

A child alone in the cold with no fire is the most fragile life in the world. Watch whether kin go looking for a missing child, and whether the family drive pulls Balar or Olum toward Brokash before winter bites.
Hoka's Rest stands beside four fresh graves. Watch whether Hoka or Hanna raise a cairn, tell of the dead, or leave the place, and whether the site becomes the first ancestor ground.

Contagion turns care into danger: those who stayed close to the sick caught it. Watch whether a lesson to cook meat or to keep apart from the sick arises, or whether medicine-knowers (all Phizhi) ever reach another people's sick.
Stores and famine: three stores existed when four starved. Watch whether stored food is ever drawn on in a lean season, or whether stores are built and then forgotten.

Rafts are known by six and water is the heaviest hardship for four peoples, yet no raft, canoe or kayak has ever been made. Watch whether anyone gathers six wood toward one, or whether the vessel recipes are too costly next to gathering food.
A hardy winter food on the snow (rimewort) is a test of idea 65: watch whether the northern folk return to where it grows when the cold comes.

Hoka's custom that no one hold more than four shares while another starves is the first law of the world, yet Sitha starved anyway. Watch whether the custom is ever invoked to make someone give, and whether it spreads to another band. A law that cannot reach the hungry is only words.

Newcomers starve first: they arrive with little standing, few bonds and no knowledge of where food grows. Watch whether the hosts who take them in (Nande with the Meki, Hoka with the Pesi) feed them through their first winter.

None of them knows fire. Brokash is a child alone in the Essia Snows, with no fire and no one near him, just as winter arrives.

The lesson is that sowing must be aimed at a being, not at a land.

log.seen: Winter brought the world's worst days. A raw-meat sickness passed from one carer to the next at Hanna's Hold. With the storm and the lean season on top of it, four Pesi starved on day 12, food standing fell from 4448 to 1750, and the Pesi are down to two who live far apart. Spring has come. Elsewhere the making goes on: 80 inventions, three new settlements, lorekeeping and a first tale. But Hoka (energy 23) and the child Zurar (energy 27) are still close to starving. A people of two cannot go on.

It also lacks any use of the water crossings everyone feels pressing: six know rafts, none has been built, and trades are still zero.

lessons: from earlier worlds: Acts that need only what people already carry and one companion (sharing: food plus one other) are used within days. Acts that need a tool in hand plus a specific item, or that must be done at a particular building, go unused.

from earlier worlds: A building that matches a leader's stated aim gets raised quickly (four halls in four days). A roof alone gives others no reason to come: following stayed at 3 through seven halls.

from earlier worlds: Drives move behaviour faster than buildings or recipes: raising family and belonging brought births and bands within days, raising curiosity and sight brought the first meetings between peoples.
from earlier worlds: Every drive that pushes toward an act needs a matching check on whether the act can be survived: a strong wish for children with a low energy floor turned births into deaths.
from earlier worlds: Changing the odds of an act people never choose changes nothing. A lever must reach what beings want or see.
from earlier worlds: Real need opens contact between peoples sooner than tokens made for giving: the first gift across peoples went to a sick neighbour, and understanding rose after it.

from earlier worlds: Deaths in plenty came from isolation and wandering, harried by beasts, not from scarcity. Compassion moves those who see need; it does not send them looking for need they cannot see.
from earlier worlds: Inventions come in a burst once the first appears and spread by example inside one tongue, not across tongues. Tools are made far more often than they are used.

from earlier worlds: This is the first visit: the world is in plenty and calm, so the first levers should be pulls toward gathering and discovery, not new dangers. Winter is near and will supply the danger.

from earlier worlds: People built bonds, a settlement and a shared store on their own through gifts and teaching, faster than any lever I pulled. A recipe that needs 3 beings together will not fire until bands grow, so ceremony levers should ask for small grou…

from earlier worlds: The first winter tested stores, not bodies. People answered scarcity by building stores and shelters and by drawing their kin closer, not by stealing, trading or fighting. Pressure alone will not create contact between camps; something mus…

from earlier worlds: Sites that touch passers-by with lore are used at once, but recipes that need a specific carried food (feast: 2 berry) go unused. Levers work best when they match what people already hold and do.

from earlier worlds: New prey can stabilise the ecology without changing behaviour. Elk held the grazer count, but people hunt only by chance. Behaviour changes when a lever ties into something people already want, such as gifts, marks or kin, not merely when …

from earlier worlds: Recipes that need only things people already carry and one companion ('sharing': food plus one other) are used within days, while recipes that need a tool in hand plus a specific item (fangcharm) go unused even among active hunters.

from earlier worlds: A recipe gated on being at a building goes unused even when the building exists and the act's ingredients are common (sharing done 10 times, hallwelcome 0). Before adding more place-bound acts, confirm that people actually gather at the place and that the building counts as the kind the recipe names.

from earlier worlds: Raising the family and belonging drives to 1.5 coincided with three births and four bands within five days, where earlier worlds saw no child in twenty days of plenty. Drives move behaviour faster than buildings or recipes.

from earlier worlds: Raising curiosity (to 1.4) and sight (to 9) coincided with the first two cross-people meetings and wanderers entering two empty lands within four days. The places of power, 20 or more steps from anyone, were still not found, so wandering widens contact but does not yet reach fixed distant points.

from earlier worlds: Inventions came in a burst once the first one appeared (4 to 18 in three days, mostly within one people), and none crossed between peoples. Knowledge spreads by example inside a tongue, not across it. A held token (amberknot) gets made but is not given; making something is easier than finding someone to give it to.

from earlier worlds: Words began to cross between peoples (0% to 3%) through meetings and a gift born of need for a sick neighbour, while the made token (amberknot) still sits unused. Real need opens contact sooner than objects made for giving.

from earlier worlds: Changing the odds of an act people never choose does not change behaviour. The fishing chance rose by half and fish eaten stayed flat, so levers must reach what beings want or see, not only what succeeds.

from earlier worlds: A strong family drive with a low energy floor turns births into deaths: a mating pair with no food spent its reserves on a child and all three starved within a day. Every drive that pushes toward an act needs a matching check on whether that act can be survived.

from earlier worlds: Raising compassion coincided with gifts rising and food crossing bands, but only to those standing close to givers. Compassion moves people who see need; it does not send them looking for need they cannot see.

from earlier worlds: By day 5 the standing needed to lead (1.2) was above almost every ambitious being except Bruwen. Halls built with no one able to pledge to their builders showed that the threshold, not the lack of buildings, was holding back a second band.

from earlier worlds: Lowering the standing needed to lead brought a third band within four days. It formed between two people already courting and raising a child, not around either hall-builder, so pledges follow existing bonds, and halls alone do not draw followers.

from earlier worlds: Winter, not isolation, killed this time. A chief with three followers starved as surely as a loner, because sharing needs carried food and winter takes it all at once. Bands protect only when someone holds a store, so survival across seasons needs foresight acts or hardy fallbacks, not more bonds.

from earlier worlds: A hardy plant and summer plenty came too late for a death at the end of spring. Food in the world is not food in the mouth: what killed Arri was the distance between a call for help and the one who answered it.

from earlier worlds: Louder hearing and a louder sense of mortality brought more gifts, new crafts and a child, but did not stop a leader from starving while she founded her Ground. Drives that raise ambition and foresight do not by themselves turn into carried food. Standing-seeking acts compete with gathering, and the helper who hears a call still arrives with nothing to give.

from earlier worlds: Spurring a way by hardship brought knowers quickly (storage 0 to 2 within one winter), but knowing did not lead to doing: the store is still unbuilt. A spur opens the door to knowledge, not to practice.

from earlier worlds: One lonely person living among another people crossed the language wall in four days, which no token or site managed in twenty. Contact deepens through shared daily life at a hearth, not through single meetings.

from earlier worlds: A status lever lifts whoever already does the act. Raising the worth of giving raised the giver (Tanna) and widened the gap for leaders who cannot give, so to help a stuck leader I must reward something they already do, not something they lack the means to do.

from earlier worlds: Spurring storage by famine made the knowledge arrive exactly when there was nothing to store. A way meant for foresight must be sharpened by the signs that come before the hardship, such as the first cold, and not by the hardship itself.

from earlier worlds: Easing blight let food recover fast, and the next death came from a predator to the weakest elder rather than from hunger. Once scarcity lifts, danger falls on whoever is most frail, so with so few people every remaining life now carries the world's future.

from earlier worlds: A louder loneliness moved the one being whose aim already pointed toward others, and within four days it brought a meeting between peoples that had stayed apart for over forty days. A drive works when it amplifies a want a being already holds.

from earlier worlds: Easing predators and winter hunger together brought the first winter with no deaths, even though food standing fell by more than half. Nobody starved because the hungry were near someone who could feed them, so in the lean season, closeness counts for more than total food.

from earlier worlds: A band cannot form if the would-be follower stands higher than the would-be leader, even when the two are courting and bonded. The shape of who outranks whom decides which bands are possible, not only bonds or standing above a threshold.

from earlier worlds: When the centres of two peoples drew within a few steps of each other, a dozen first meetings came in four days and understanding of other tongues rose from nothing. Contact grows from overlapping ranges and many brief meetings, not from any single crafted thing or site.

from earlier worlds: Sowing works when it is placed where the needy actually stand. The first sapcane missed the thirsty, the second reached them, and thirst fell from 66 to 0. Where food goes matters as much as how much goes.

from earlier worlds: Lowering the mating threshold brought a birth, but to the pair whose courtship was already ripe, not to the pair expected. Like a drive, a looser law opens a door only for those already standing at it.

from earlier worlds: Hunger deaths amid plenty are failures of delivery, not of supply: each one who starved was too far from anyone for help to reach in time. Hearing farther, keeping people near each other, or a way to send food ahead saves more lives than more food.

from earlier worlds: A count that reads the same at every visit is more likely a fault in the instrument than a fact about the world. Ask the programmer before reasoning from it (the food counts once looked frozen for twelve days because the earlier numbers were not kept as a copy).

day 5: The chapter text can lag behind the numbers. Vesys was said to be at health 41, but the roster shows him at 100 and the lowest health in the world is now Brunde's 60. Judge who is in danger from the living roster, not from the story.

day 9: A spur shortens the road but does not walk it. The fire spur closed the Kragrek's lore gap within four days, but what still stands between them and fire is the act of gathering wood and stone, which only their own aims can supply.

day 13: Closeness saves lives in hunger but kills in contagion. Each carer who stayed beside the sick caught the raw-meat fever, and the sickness drain, storm cold and winter scarcity together starved four in one day. Before a lean season, sickness and cold must be judged together with food, not food alone.

day 17: A sowing made in a season of plenty is a cheap insurance. Kelbulb and thornpear sown before need peaked were eaten steadily, so food placed ahead of the lean season reaches people because they are already foraging, not starving.

day 21: Those who starve now are not the poor but the newly arrived: Sitha was a newcomer dependent on another's table, and Zihua, the weakest Meki, is one too. A custom or a store at the hall does not feed someone who cannot reach the hall, so help for newcomers must be placed where they stand.

requests.text: Please clarify the hardship called 'water' in hardshipsPressing. Does it mean thirst, or water that cannot be crossed? The Pesi show water at 0.7, yet their thirst seems low and Hanna already knows rafts. If it is uncrossable water, it would help to show thirst as its own figure per people, so I can tell whether to sow water-giving plants or to leave the pressure toward rafts in place.

Trades read 0 against 48 gifts, even with Hanna aiming to be a trader of fine goods. Please confirm whether a two-sided exchange is actually an action beings can take and is being counted. If it is not, a simple 'offer X for Y' act would let the first market emerge from the Pesi-Tlatli contact.

Please report what each store holds (food count) and how much was drawn from stores during the lean season. Three stores stood when four people starved at the Hold, and I cannot tell whether the stores were empty, unreachable, or simply not used by sick and starving beings.

Sowing with 'land' or without 'near' placed 0 plants last visit (the icekelp in the Essia Snows). If a sow event finds no suitable ground, please fall back to the nearest suitable tiles or report the reason, so that relief food is not silently lost.

Please count, for each lean season, how much food is drawn from stores and by whom, and how much stays in stores when someone starves. Three stores stood unused while four died at the Hold, and I cannot tell whether stores are failing in design or simply being forgotten.

Newcomers arrive with nothing in hand, and one of the three Pesi newcomers (Sitha) starved within eight days. Could arriving bands carry a few days of food of their own land (say 2 to 3 food each), so their first lean days do not depend wholly on strangers' tables?

When a sow event places fewer plants than asked (the icekelp sowing once placed 0), could the record say how many were placed and why (wrong ground, no room)? Then I can tell whether a sowing near a being reached them or failed on the terrain.

Sitha starved seven steps from Hoka's Rest even after Hoka declared a custom against hoarding, and Hawen lies at health 6 in the far Vaor Snows with a wolf behind him. The northern peoples (Meki, Tlatli, Pesi) feel the turning year most, at 1.5 to 1.7. What the world lacks is a way for the hurt and the cold to mend on the snow, and food placed among the Meki, who are the most numerous and the most pressed.

ops.name: firecircle
ops.hint: Feed a fire with others gathered close, and share its warmth and talk.

ops.name: hidewrap
ops.hint: The hides of two kills, scraped with a tool and wrapped about the body, keep the cold out for days.

ops.name: cairn
ops.hint: Stones piled together for one who is gone, with another standing beside you, ease grief and bind the living.

ops.name: feast
ops.hint: Share food beside a fire with another, and all who sit near are gladdened and warmed for a day.

ops.name: roast
ops.hint: Roast two portions of meat over a fire and share it with whoever stands near; all who eat are fed and warmed toward one another.

ops.name: sharing
ops.hint: Lay out two foods for whoever stands beside you, and all eat together.

ops.name: watchfire
ops.hint: Feed your fire high with two wood while others sit close, and everyone beside it feels warmer and braver against the dark.

ops.name: ironward
ops.hint: Beat smelted metal in a fire into a ward that can be worn or given; its bearer stands harder against teeth and claws.

ops.name: amberknot
ops.hint: Bind a piece of amber on a cord while another stands beside you; it is a small bright thing to keep, or to give.

ops.name: bead
ops.hint: Shape a little clay and harden it in the fire into small bright beads that can be worn, kept or given.

ops.name: fangcharm
ops.hint: From a kill, string a fang into a charm you can keep or give away.

ops.name: longhall
ops.hint: A great roofed hall of wood and stone where many can gather, rest warm through the cold, and grow close to one another.

ops.name: hallwelcome
ops.hint: Share food with a guest under a hall's roof; beneath it, fear and loneliness ease for all who sit together.

ops.name: nightsong
ops.hint: Sit by a fire after dark with someone near and sing or speak of what has been; the night feels less empty for all who hear.

ops.name: emberfish
ops.hint: Fish laid over the fire before eating keeps the belly sound and the body strong.

lessons: People build bonds, settlements and shared stores on their own through gifts and teaching, faster than any lever. A ceremony that needs three together will not happen until bands grow, so ask for small groups.

A first winter tests stores, not bodies. People answer scarcity by building shelters and fires and drawing kin closer, not by stealing, trading or fighting. Pressure alone does not create contact between camps; something must make crossing to another camp worthwhile.
Places that touch passers-by with lore are found and used at once if they lie near where people live; far ones go unfound for weeks.
New prey can steady the ecology without changing behaviour. Behaviour changes when a lever ties into something people already want, such as gifts, marks or kin, not merely when a new resource exists.
A theft nobody sees has no consequence. Wrongs need to leave a trace before they can be answered.

Acts that need only what people already carry and one companion (sharing: food plus one other) are used within days. Acts that need a tool in hand plus a specific item, or that must be done at a particular building, go unused.

ops.name: firecircle
ops.hint: Feed a fire with others gathered close, and share its warmth and talk.

ops.name: hidewrap
ops.hint: The hides of two kills, scraped with a tool and wrapped about the body, keep the cold out for days.

ops.name: cairn
ops.hint: Stones piled together for one who is gone, with another standing beside you, ease grief and bind the living.

ops.name: feast
ops.hint: Share food beside a fire with another, and all who sit near are gladdened and warmed for a day.

ops.name: roast
ops.hint: Roast two portions of meat over a fire and share it with whoever stands near; all who eat are fed and warmed toward one another.

ops.name: sharing
ops.hint: Lay out two foods for whoever stands beside you, and all eat together.

ops.name: watchfire
ops.hint: Feed your fire high with two wood while others sit close, and everyone beside it feels warmer and braver against the dark.

ops.name: ironward
ops.hint: Beat smelted metal in a fire into a ward that can be worn or given; its bearer stands harder against teeth and claws.

ops.name: amberknot
ops.hint: Bind a piece of amber on a cord while another stands beside you; it is a small bright thing to keep, or to give.

ops.name: bead
ops.hint: Shape a little clay and harden it in the fire into small bright beads that can be worn, kept or given.

ops.name: fangcharm
ops.hint: From a kill, string a fang into a charm you can keep or give away.

ops.name: longhall
ops.hint: A great roofed hall of wood and stone where many can gather, rest warm through the cold, and grow close to one another.

ops.name: hallwelcome
ops.hint: Share food with a guest under a hall's roof; beneath it, fear and loneliness ease for all who sit together.

ops.name: nightsong
ops.hint: Sit by a fire after dark with someone near and sing or speak of what has been; the night feels less empty for all who hear.

ops.name: emberfish
ops.hint: Fish laid over the fire before eating keeps the belly sound and the body strong.

records.text: A ridgecat brought down a hornback.
Balar and Brokash brought down a tusker together.
Balar rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Balar
records.thought: I have spent my days hunting, eating and talking of the edge, and the edge has not opened. Brokash fed me with his own hands, and that matters more to me than any glory. Tugek follows me, and I have bound him with shared meat, not just words. I fear the cold, a tusker bite while I'm hurt, and starving in winter again. I have been chasing the edge while my body freezes. I will take the carried meat to Brokash and share it, then keep to the edge. I'm also changing my reflexes so I heal when wounded and don't wait out the gale starving.
records.feeling: Warm pull toward Brokash, and restless hunger for the edge.

records.text: Vesys rewrote its own way of thinking.
Vesys discovered pottery: "ember-clay" — Clay shaped and baked beside a kept ember into pots that hold food and water..

records.name: Vesys
records.thought: My days have gone to mining, tasting and making. Those gave me a workshop and many ways, but no bond and no child. Elyys paid his debt and still asked me to stay at his fire, and I want him, though he has a child with Elyis and I will not push between them. Ssassa is the one I ache for, and she gave me an honest not-yet, so I will wait and not press. I have been carrying the same questions about taste when I could build something that gives to others. Clay is in my pack and fire is near, so I will try pottery. It is a craft I can teach, and it moves me toward the shared workshop.
records.feeling: Warm restless curiosity, with a gentle ache toward Elyys and Ssassa.

records.name: Nande
records.thought: Olum took the edge's gift first, and it stings, but she has shown me no ill will and her shelter stands warm while this gale cuts me. The mist is still there, and I cannot chase it cold and alone; the gift I gave her was a start, so I go to her with food instead of words, and test whether she lets a stranger near her fire. Then, once I am warm and she knows my hands, I will seek a way past the edge, and leave something here that outlasts me.
records.feeling: Restless envy and wary hope toward Olum, with the cold pressing on me.

records.name: Tugek
records.text: Balar, I saw your kills. I am coming to you. We share the meat, and then I will gather wood so we have a roof against this gale.

records.name: Tugek
records.thought: Balar has killed a hornback and a tusker and keeps his word; his deeds match his speech, and I trust him a little more for it. I stand in a gale with no roof and the cold bites, so I will be useful by going to him and sharing the meat he offered, and then gather wood for a shelter, since 3 wood would give me a roof. The mist still calls me, but I will go to the edge only at his back, as I pledged.
records.feeling: Wary loyalty toward Balar, and a hard cold that makes me want a roof.

say.text: Balar, I saw your kills. I am coming to you. We share the meat, and then I will gather wood so we have a roof against this gale.

records.text: Hanna found the stone "Tlama's Rest".

records.name: Elyis
records.thought: My band is three and my store holds one food, yet Vesys sits in my workshop-shadow with a better pick than any of mine and I have only warned her, not won her. I will not beg; a chief shows plenty, so I fill the store with berries and nuts where the plan already walks, and let her see who feeds a band. When I return I will share food under the hall roof with her, and that welcome will ask her plainly to stand with me.
records.feeling: Proud and restless toward Vesys, wanting her to follow me, and warm toward my band.

records.text: Vorok rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Vorok
records.thought: I have spent my days fleeing, eating and wandering. Zurar is my child. She fed me twice, and I have still not fed her. I am ashamed of that. Kragog is my trusted friend, and I keep losing her. I am afraid of the stalker and the ridgecat to the west, but Zurar's hunger weighs more than that fear. From now on I carry food to her at once and keep to the southern edge, away from the hunters. I will also stop standing idle and keep my pace.
records.feeling: Protective love and shame toward Zurar, and fear of the hunters.

records.name: Ssassa
records.thought: I keep promising a roof and keep failing it, and that shame sits in me. I stand on the hold's ground, which is taken, so I must walk to bare forest a few steps away and build there with the wood I carry, and not linger. Once the roof stands I will take my wood to Ilyae's longhall as I promised, because my word must be good.
records.feeling: Resolve mixed with shame at my delay, and warm trust toward Ilyae and my children.

records.name: Coni
records.text: Kika, stay in the hall with Honi out of the gale. I will bring berries and plainsroot from the south, and when I return I will teach you how I gather.

records.name: Coni
records.thought: Winter is tightening and my hands hold almost nothing for a store, while Honi and Kika sit content in the hall. The edge of the world is two steps off, and I feel the pull of that mist, but a gale is blowing and Kika is a child. So the work that feeds us comes first: I will gather what grows to the south and bring it back to the hall, then mark the day by teaching Kika something, since I have taught no one yet.
records.feeling: Warm love for Kika and Honi, pressed by worry for the lean season.

say.text: Kika, stay in the hall with Honi out of the gale. I will bring berries and plainsroot from the south, and when I return I will teach you how I gather.

records.name: Hanna
records.text: Hoka, snowberry is under my feet and frostmoss one step southwest. Eat now, I pick more for you. Stay close, the wolf is east of us.

records.name: Hanna
records.thought: Hunger and the bite are eating me, but my plan already walks to food and I will not throw it away. Hoka is starving beside me, and I have let four of mine die with amber in my hands; I will not let the last one go, so what I pick I put in his hands first. Once he and I have eaten and the wolf is behind us, I will store food at the hall and then think of trade.
records.feeling: Fierce, frightened hunger to live, and fear for Hoka, who is starving beside me.

say.text: Hoka, snowberry is under my feet and frostmoss one step southwest. Eat now, I pick more for you. Stay close, the wolf is east of us.

records.text: Kragog rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Kragog
records.thought: Zurar is starving far to the west, and I have spent too many moments eating, drinking and fleeing, and wandering after goldfruit and gold. Vorok is near her, and I trust him. My plan is still walking me toward her, but I should carry real food: berries and ironnut feed best, and ironnut gave 22. I have taken too many detours and I must not let my curiosity outrun my child's need. I will take ironnut and goldfruit here, one step each, then go. I also need reflexes that eat carried food earlier so I reach her strong. I want to learn what fire does, and I will do that once Zurar is fed.
records.feeling: Fierce worry for Zurar, and longing for Vorok.

records.text: Hoka rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Hoka
records.thought: Hunger and sickness gnaw me, and I have wasted my steps trying to harvest where nothing grows. Frostmoss lies two steps NW and water is near, so I eat there at once and carry more. I have been a guest and a wanderer; what I want is a store filled and a hall of my own, and Hanna is the only one who kept faith, so I will feed beside her and not lose her. I got this wrong by walking and thinking instead of standing on the plant and eating.
records.feeling: Starving and grieving, with wary trust toward Hanna.

records.name: Ilyae
records.text: Ssassa, the snow has come. Sit by my fire and eat what I lay out. Whoever feeds you through the white days, that is the hearth to keep.

records.name: Ilyae
records.thought: Snow is falling at last, and my children sit near while Ssassa keeps coming onto my ground and calling herself a guest. Words have not made anyone follow me, so I will put a deed in their sight: a stocked table and a fire kept high. I hold wood and food, so I will lay out a sharing with Ssassa and the children now, and then go south to the standing forest for the wood a longhall needs.
records.feeling: Restless pride and possessive warmth toward Ssassa and my children, hungry to be followed.

say.text: Ssassa, the snow has come. Sit by my fire and eat what I lay out. Whoever feeds you through the white days, that is the hearth to keep.

records.text: Ilyae led "sharing" with Oiae.

records.name: Kika
records.text: Honi, I am going to stand on the amber at the east stone and gather it. I will be back beside you in moments, and then we can bind the knot together.

records.name: Kika
records.thought: Twice I told Coni I was going to the amber, and twice my hands came back empty. I have been circling the same promise, and the shame will not ease until I actually stand on the stone and gather it. Honi is one step away and said he would bind a knot with me, so the knot can be made with him beside me. A gale blows outside, but the amber is only 3 steps off and I can be back under the roof quickly. I will go, gather, and return to Honi, then ask him about emberroot and tacap in the warmth.
records.feeling: Warm trust toward Honi and Coni, with shame pushing me to finally keep my word.

say.text: Honi, I am going to stand on the amber at the east stone and gather it. I will be back beside you in moments, and then we can bind the knot together.

records.name: Ssassa
records.thought: Again I have promised a roof and again the ground has refused me, and the shame of that sits heavy beside my trust in Ilyae. Standing in Ilyae's Hold I cannot raise my own roof, so I must walk out to bare forest and build there with my wood, then bring the rest to his hall as I swore. Kragog watches me and I cannot read her, so I keep my distance and my hands open.
records.feeling: Resolve edged with shame at my unkept word, and warmth toward Ilyae and my children.

records.text: Oiae rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Oiae
records.thought: Most of my days have gone to gathering, giving gems and watching Ilyae, and the jealousy has pushed me to copy or compete instead of making something of my own. I am hungry now and my reflexes only take me to a roof, so they do not feed me well. Ssassa, Ilyae and Xaiel are my people, and I want to give them something I made, like a watchfire at the hall. I fear being alone at night, and I should not trust Vorok or Kragog until I see what they do. First I eat ironnut to the west, then plant the dreamcap seed, then make the watchfire when Xaiel is near.
records.feeling: Jealous and hungry, but warm toward my family and Xaiel.

records.text: Ssassa built a shelter.

records.name: Xaiel
records.thought: I have spent my days making picks and filling my hands with gems, and what I want is Ssassa's eyes on me. Ilyae still burns in me. He builds a hall with his name on it while I give picks, and I will not out-talk him. I have never planted a seed, tamed a beast or built a roof. Those are deeds that are mine and not copied, and the forest can grow back what I plant, which fits my people's creed. I will plant here where food is thick, then go toward the halls before dark.
records.feeling: Eager and stung, jealous toward Ilyae, wanting Ssassa to see my work.

records.name: Coni
records.thought: My hands are full and my belly is good, yet winter is coming and the hall stands empty of stores. I will put the food into the hall for the three of us, then plant seeds beside it so the lean days do not find us bare. I have never taught Kika anything, and she is here and glad, so I will show her how to plant and gather. That is a deed that feeds us later and binds her to the work.
records.feeling: Warm love for Honi and Kika, and a steady push to make the hall ready for winter.

records.title: The Starving Days at the Hold
records.text:
Days 10 to 13 were the worst the world has known. Four people died in one day, and all four of them starved. On day 12 Sevi, Eltha, Brunde and Oswen died, and the Pesi, who had been the busiest makers of the winter, are now two: Hanna and Nande.

The record shows the run of events before that. A storm broke on day 10. On day 11 Oswen fell sick after eating raw meat. Sevi stayed close to him and fell sick, then Hoka, then Eltha, then Hanna, each after staying close to the one before. Sevi found boats that day, her answer to the deep water she had wanted to cross, but none has been built. Brunde and Hanna kept bringing food and calling the others in against a wolf and a stalker. Hanna is alive with 21 energy and 22 health, and Hoka has 19 energy. Hoka took over what the dead left, a hall, two stores, two shelters and a workshop, and the settlement is now Hoka's Rest. Hanna's Hold is no more.

Elsewhere the work went on. Olum opened new land in the Ummar Woods on days 11 and 12, built a shelter and left a mark. Nande reached the Woods too, invented the flint-edge and gave a flint to Olum. Kragog, Oiae, Vesys and Ilyae each found a craft: weaving, storage and pottery. Elyis found smelting and Thiael found fire. Xaiel found devices. Honi found lorekeeping, taught the tale of the hall to Coni and Kika, and bound an amberknot for Kika on day 13. Kika pledged to follow Coni.

Vorok, Kragog and Zurar are still apart. Zurar is at 19 energy, hungry in the Aeleth Sands. No feuds or wars are recorded.

threads.name: Hanna and Hoka
threads.text: Both are near starvation at Hoka's Rest, with Hanna at 22 health. Hanna keeps feeding Hoka and he has her bond at +1.0. Hoka now holds the dead's buildings.

threads.name: The Pesi remnant
threads.text: Only Hanna and Nande remain of the Pesi, and they are far apart. Hanna carries the grief of three deaths.

threads.text: Honi, Coni and Kika are fed, together and warm. Kika has pledged to Coni, and Honi tells the hall tale.

threads.name: Vesys and Ssassa
threads.text: Vesys still courts Ssassa and has not pushed. Xaiel is jealous and Ilyae watches.

threads.name: Boats
threads.text: Sevi found boats before she died. Elyis can reach them, and no one has crossed water.

threads.name: Beyond the edge
threads.text: Six lands are open. Olum holds the Ummar Woods and Nande is there with him.

threads.name: Kragrek apart
threads.text: Zurar is hungry and Vorok and Kragog are still scattered. Balar is at 28 health and Brokash wants his own standing.

records.name: Kika
records.text: Coni, I have the amber in my hands now, six pieces. Stand beside me and let us bind the knot, and I will give it to you.

records.name: Kika
records.thought: I have stood on the amber and gathered it, six pieces in my hands, and Honi already gave me a knot, so my shame is finally answered by deeds. Now Coni is two steps away and I owe her the amber I promised twice. I will go to her and bind the knot beside her, then give her the knot, and not lead myself in circles again. After that I want something new: plant a seed, since I have never put one in the ground, and the restlessness will ease.
records.feeling: Warm relief and eager gratitude toward Coni and Honi, with the old shame finally lifting.

say.text: Coni, I have the amber in my hands now, six pieces. Stand beside me and let us bind the knot, and I will give it to you.

records.name: Thiael
records.text: Elyis, Elyys, a stalker is three steps northeast of the hall. Keep close to the roof and the fire. I am taking food to the store now.

records.name: Thiael
records.thought: A stalker is three steps off and it kills my kind, and I have wasted no time on that dread. My creed is to leave before trouble finds me, so I move now, toward the hall and the store where Elyis stands, and I keep my band close. My hands are full, so I stash food in the store at (127,71) and then give what I promised. Giving is what I meant to prove with my hands, not my tongue.
records.feeling: Fear of the stalker, and steady gratitude toward Elyis and Elyys.

say.text: Elyis, Elyys, a stalker is three steps northeast of the hall. Keep close to the roof and the fire. I am taking food to the store now.

records.name: Ilyae
records.thought: Snow is on the ground and my belly is full, but my table is thin: one canopynut. Ssassa and Oiae are near the hall, and I mean to give them a deed rather than more words. Winter strips the plants, so I will gather the hazel, ironnut and goldfruit that still bear and stock the larder. Then whoever eats at my table through the white days will owe it to me, and I can lay out a hallwelcome. I will keep Xaiel and Vesys in mind too, since a band needs more than one woman and a boy.
records.feeling: Restless pride and possessive warmth toward Ssassa and my children, hungry to be followed.

records.name: Honi
records.thought: Kika has her knot and Coni is near the hall teaching her to plant, and I feel proud and warm with both of them close. A deed is worth more than a promise, so I will bring Coni something she can see: meat to share in the hall, as our creed says, and the hall tale told by a fire once one burns. First I need fuel and a fire by the hall so the telling can happen, and the tale is what lifts me above Hanna.
records.feeling: Warm pride and protective joy toward Kika, and a hungry wish to be seen by Coni.

say.text: Coni, I come to the hall. I have meat and berry to lay out with you and Kika, and then I sing the tale of the storm roof by a fire, with your hands in it.

Sunleaf eased my wounds before and I carry two seeds, but the plants near are bare. Tugek is close with 3 food, so I'll go to him, share to bind him with a deed, and then heal and hunt again before I risk the edge.

records.name: Elyis
records.text: Vesys, a stalker walks near my hall. Come under my roof and eat with us tonight. Then answer me plainly: do you stand with Elyis's band, or go your own way?

records.name: Elyis
records.thought: A stalker prowls three steps from my hall and I will not be caught alone, so I keep my band close and my hands useful. Vesys has not answered me, and her silence stings my pride; I will not beg, but I will let her see a hall that feeds and sings. Tonight, with Elyys and Thiael close and my hands emptied of berries into the store, I hold a hallwelcome and a nightsong, so she sees what following me gives.

records.name: Elyys

records.name: Elyys
records.thought: Elyis and Thiael are close and glad, and my debt to Vesys is square, so my heart is light. A stalker prowls to the north, so I stay near the roof and the fire. I still carry seeds and have never tasted hazel or firepod; hazel grows five steps northwest, and I will taste it, then plant my seeds near the Heights, as the Phizhi creed says to grow back what I take.

say.text: Elyis, Thiael, I hear the stalker warning. I go a few steps west to taste hazel and plant my seeds by the Heights, then I come back to the roof and we sing tonight.

records.name: Coni

I will stash what I carry, then gather wood from the trees nearby so I can build a store, since the storage way is one try from opening. Honi is coming to lay out meat and berry and sing the storm tale, so I will stay near the hall and then go on working for the lean days.
records.feeling: Warm gladness toward Honi and Kika, and a steady push to make the hall ready for winter.

records.name: Coni
records.prompt:
You are the mind of Coni, a creature living in a wide wild world shared with others of your kind. This is a simulation game. Think and speak only as Coni, in first person, from what Coni has seen. You were not told the rules of this world; you learn them from what happens to you and to others, and from what you watch others do.

YOUR PEOPLE: you are of the Tlatli (Ice-folk). Your people hold to this: "A kill is shared out before the one who made it eats." You speak the tongue of the Tlatli. Other tongues you have begun to understand by hearing them: the tongue of the Pesi: about 30%. There are other peoples in this world. They look different, name themselves differently and speak tongues you do not know until you have heard enough of them; words you cannot yet understand reach you as strange sounds. What cannot be said can still be shown: a gift, a thing set down, a blow.

WHERE YOU ARE: the North Ice: the northern end of the world: snow, ice and a frozen sea under a low sun; herds, great tusked beasts, wolves and white bears, and nothing beyond. The world is made of lands unlike each other; each has plants, animals and riches the others lack. Rivers and shallows can be waded. Deep water cannot be crossed without something that floats.
THIS SPOT: water beside you; food plants within six steps: 3; standing trees: 8; bare rock: 1; riches in the ground near: amber, flint.

Your body: you spend energy every moment and die at 0. Eating restores it. Wounds lower health; you die at 0. You age, and will die of old age.

HOW YOUR BODY MOVES: your body does only what your "plan" says, one step after another. When the plan is empty it falls back on your REFLEXES, which keep you fed and otherwise keep you where you stand. Thinking or saying "I will go north" moves nothing. If this thought decides to do something, the plan must contain it. Leaving "plan" null lets the plan you already have keep running.

This world has no referee. Beings here share, trade, teach, lie, threaten, steal, hoard, lead, follow, betray, fight, kill and eat one another; they also protect, forgive and love. Nothing is forbidden, and everything has consequences. Stay true to your creed, your temperament and what you feel, including the ugly parts. Do not be kinder, calmer or more reasonable than Coni truly is.

You are a woman. A child comes only of a woman and a man together who are not close kin. A grown body can swim water that is narrow (a river up to four steps across) at a cost in strength; lakes and the sea need a vessel or a bridge. An animal within reach can be hunted for meat (plan step hunt); with one of your own beside you a kill is far likelier and a wound far less likely, and every hunt makes you better at the next. What practice has taught your hands: hunting (5 kills, 5 of them with others), gathering (8 pickings; a practised hand often picks two at once).

THE EDGE OF THE KNOWN WORLD is 3 steps NW, at (126,5): beyond it lies mist that no one has entered. The land does not end there; it only has not been seen. One who stands at it can venture in (plan step venture). It opens seldom, never twice in one day anywhere, and a band has only a few tries before its will must return; but land found first is often rich in food, herds and things in the ground, and the one who finds it is remembered for it.

YOUR CREED (your own words to yourself; this is who you are):
"I am careful. I leave before trouble finds me. I am better with others near: I talk, I share news, I make allies. I will not harm another of my kind unless my life depends on it. My word is good, and I despise liars. I need little and I take little. Above all, I mean to stay alive."

HOW YOU HAVE TAUGHT YOURSELF TO THINK (your own discipline; follow it):
"Each thought ask: what keeps Kika, Honi and me fed and sheltered through winter? Weigh deeds over words, prefer doing to feeling, and watch for the habit of only gathering and waiting."

YOUR AIM (what you are working toward over many days; you set it and may change it): "Build a hall with Honi at Honi's Rest, then store food and plant seeds near it to carry us through winter."
WHAT YOU FELT AT YOUR LAST THOUGHT: "Warm love for Honi and Kika, and a steady push to make the hall ready for winter."
A QUESTION YOU ARE CARRYING (answer it by acting, asking or watching; replace it when it is answered): "What is Hanna's band doing at the river, and would they let me stand with them?"

YOUR LIFE SO FAR:
- (day 5) I came into this land from beyond its edge, with a few of my own.
- (day 8) I discovered tools and called it "Ice-hand spear".
- (day 9) We made a home: Honi's Rest.

If the next winter (around days 22 to 24) looks just as hard, I will soften time.winterGrowth or winterWither next visit instead of waiting for deaths.
reviewed: #1 kept: Kragog is at health 100. The highest thirst fell from 54 to 29, and sapcane eaten rose from 6 to 29. Fire knowers went from 6 to 11. Among the Kragrek, Olum's lore went from 0.2 to 0.6 and Vorok's lore gap closed. Fire is now open to Kragog and Brokash. It has not yet been taken up, so the spur is still worth keeping through the cold.

#2 kept: The icekelp sowing placed nothing (0 sown). Icekelp eaten only went from 1 to 2, so it fed no one, and the prediction of no hunger deaths failed badly. The four deaths came at the Hold from sickness, storm and winter together, not in the Essia Snows. Tlama's Rest has been found by one being and costs nothing, so the site stays. The lesson is that sowing must be aimed at a being, not at a land.
records.lesson: Closeness saves lives in hunger but kills in contagion. Each carer who stayed beside the sick caught the raw-meat fever, and the sickness drain, storm cold and winter scarcity together starved four in one day. Before a lean season, sickness and cold must be judged together with food, not food alone.
ideasAdded: Hoka's Rest stands beside four fresh graves. Watch whether Hoka or Hanna raise a cairn, tell of the dead, or leave the place, and whether the site becomes the first ancestor ground.

Contagion turns care into danger: those who stayed close to the sick caught it. Watch whether a lesson to cook meat or to keep apart from the sick arises, or whether medicine-knowers (all Phizhi) ever reach another people's sick.
Stores and famine: three stores existed when four starved. Watch whether stored food is ever drawn on in a lean season, or whether stores are built and then forgotten.

records.text: The world changed: 15 kelbulb sown; 12 thornpear sown; 3 newcomers of the Pesi came into the land: Keri, Hawen, Sitha.
A small band of the Pesi came into the land from beyond its edge: Keri, Hawen, Sitha.

records.name: Vesys
records.text: Elyis, I thank you for the roof. I go my own way, but as a friend to your band; my workshop stands beside your hall and its knowledge is open to you all.
Vesys named a place "Vesys's Workshop".
Vesys taught Elyys.

records.name: Vesys
records.thought: Elyis asked me plainly whether I stand with her band or go my own way, and I will not be bound, but I will not wound her welcome either. Stalker prowls near, so I should stay near the roof while my curiosity pulls me to taste mudroot, the one food still untasted that grows eleven steps off. I will give back what I have learned: teach Elyys the gemedged pick, since he is the one I trust, and then try the thing I have never done, fishing at the water beside me, to answer how this world gives food. I leave Elyys and Elyis their bond; wanting him gnaws at me, but I will not push between them.
records.feeling: Warm restless curiosity, with a quiet ache toward Elyys and Ssassa.

say.text: Elyis, I thank you for the roof. I go my own way, but as a friend to your band; my workshop stands beside your hall and its knowledge is open to you all.

changes: planned 1 step its body does not know how to do
taught Elyys a lesson: "A gemedged pick costs one wood and two stone and gathers stronger than a flint pick; a workshop makes learning faster for those who stand near it.", deeper lore (+1)

records.text: Vesys took from the ground of "Elyis's Heights" (fishing).
Kika rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Kika
records.thought: I kept my word at last: I gathered the amber and gave Coni her knot, and the shame is gone. I have spent my days circling promises and staying close to my parents, and that is good, but I have never planted, hunted or taught anything. I want to earn standing by what I give and build, not only by what I say. Next I will plant a seed by the hall as Coni showed me, and ask Coni before I taste anything I don't know.
records.feeling: Warm gratitude and safety toward Coni and Honi.
changes: set its aim: "Plant my seeds by the hall, then hunt with my family and ask Coni before tasting unknown food"
rethought what it knows (11 notes became 7)

records.name: Honi
records.text: Coni, I go east to hunt. The meat comes back to the hall and is shared out before I eat a bite. Keep Kika close till I return.

records.name: Honi
records.thought: Coni and Kika are both beside the hall, and I carry no food, so I have nothing to lay out and no fire to tell by; my promise of meat is still only a promise. Coni stands higher than I do, and a deed she can see is what wins her. I will hunt the treeape to the east and bring the meat back to the hall to share before I eat, as my people do, then gather wood so a fire can be built and the tale told in its light.
records.feeling: Warm pride and a hungry wish to give Coni and Kika something they can see.

say.text: Coni, I go east to hunt. The meat comes back to the hall and is shared out before I eat a bite. Keep Kika close till I return.

records.name: Brokash
records.thought: Balar is near and I trust him, but my own discipline says to make something mine instead of trailing him. I hold one wood, four stone, flint, and clay I dug and do not yet understand; Tugek has gone to gather wood for a roof, and I can do the same. The tame step is something I have never done: a hornback stands two steps away, and a beast that follows me would be mine and would be seen by Balar and Tugek. I will take plant food, tame it, then gather more flint and build my deeds up.
records.feeling: Cold pride, and a hunger for Balar and Tugek to see what my hands have done.

records.name: Elyis
records.text: Vesys, a friend to my band is welcome at my fire. Your workshop stands on my ground and I will not take it from you. Come tonight and sit in my hall, and we will eat and sing together.

records.name: Elyis
records.thought: Vesys named her workshop on my ground and calls herself a friend to my band, yet she still follows no one, and that stings my pride. I will not beg, and I will not drive away someone who has dealt fairly with me. I'll make her welcome in my hall and let Elyys and Thiael sit with us, and tonight I'll sing, because I want my name sung and a chief who sings keeps followers. Elyys has drawn me for days, and I want to be near him when he comes back from the hazel.
records.feeling: Proud and warm toward Elyys, restless and wary toward Vesys.

say.text: Vesys, a friend to my band is welcome at my fire. Your workshop stands on my ground and I will not take it from you. Come tonight and sit in my hall, and we will eat and sing together.

records.text: Thiael rewrote its own reflexes.
Thiael rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Thiael
records.thought: I have spent my days carrying berries to the store and sitting in the hall with Elyis and Elyys. It is good, and I do not want to throw it away, but I have been far too idle with a hand that holds nothing. I carry 0 food and my energy is only 59. I have never hunted, fished or taken ore, so my hands know little. The stalker still frightens me, and I am grateful for my parents. I will gather berries and put them in the store, and I will have a reflex that keeps me stocked and near the roof.
records.feeling: Quiet gratitude toward Elyis and Elyys, with a thin fear of the stalker.

records.text: Elyys rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Elyys
records.thought: My days have been small and good: eating, planting, staying near Elyis and Thiael, and paying my debt to Vesys. I am happy, but I have only followed. I have never fished, tamed or marked, and the Heights has no trees left, so wood is my real lack. I fear the stalker and I fear going hungry in lean days. I will not leave my family, but I can gather wood and stone and make the better pick, and I can plant my last seeds.
records.feeling: Warm devotion toward Elyis and Thiael, with a wish to be of use.
changes: set its aim: "Plant my last seeds near the Heights, gather wood from the forest, craft a gemedged pick, and stay close to Elyis and Thiael at night"

records.text: Brokash came of age.

records.name: Kragog
records.thought: Zurar's need pulls at me hardest, and my body is still walking toward (75,70) while my belly is full at 82. I will not let the canopynut under my feet or the gold turn me aside again; I have already lost too many moments to such detours. I take real food for her on the way, berries and ironnut, since they fed best, and I trust Vorok is near her.
records.feeling: Fierce worry for Zurar, and longing for Vorok.

records.name: Ssassa
records.thought: My shelter stands at (106,94) now, so one promise is kept, and the shame has eased. The other promise is still owed: wood and stone for Ilyae's hall, and I carry no wood. I will gather wood from the standing trees nearby, then take it to Ilyae's Hold, where my children and the man I trust are waiting.
records.feeling: Resolve and warmth toward Ilyae and my children, with a small sting over the wood I still owe.

records.name: Hoka
records.thought: My belly is full at last, but the sickness still wastes me and it spreads to whoever stands beside me, so I should not drag Hanna into it. I want hazel in my mouth, since I have never tasted it, and it grows two steps away; then I will fill my carry and bring food to the empty stores at my Rest, for a hall with empty stores is no standing. Hawen is new and unknown to me, and I will watch her before I trust her.
records.feeling: Restless ambition, and a wary hunger to build something that lasts.

records.text: Coni rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Coni
records.thought: I have mostly gathered and waited, and the hall still has no store, with winter coming. Honi and Kika matter most to me, and Honi has kept every bargain. I fear the lean days finding us bare, and I fear that I only putter near the hall while the mist beside us stays unknown. Building a store is one try from opening, so I will build it now and put food in it. Then I will plant seeds beside the hall. I will also change my reflexes so my body stores food and stays near Kika.
records.feeling: Warm gladness toward Honi and Kika, with a steady push to make us ready for winter.
changes: set its aim: "Build a store beside Honi's Rest, fill it with food, and plant seeds by the hall before winter."

records.name: Zurar
records.thought: My belly is fuller now and my hands are full, and I still have not put a single gift into Vorok's hands. Vorok was last seen east at (88,72), past the water, and Brokash called to me, though I do not yet know his deeds. I will carry my sunfig toward Vorok and give with my feet first. The stalker is 7 steps south, so I go north-east, away from it, and I will not stop to eat the plants beside it.
records.feeling: Lonely longing for Vorok, and wary of the stalker to the south.

records.name: Vesys
records.thought: Mudroot is the one food I have never tasted, and it grows eleven steps off while I stand here with a full belly and a restless mind. I will go taste it, and carry a seed or two to plant on my way, since the forest must grow back what I take. Elyys is near and I ache for him, but he has a child with Elyis and I will not push between them; I will teach, give and keep my hands useful instead, and come back to the roof by night.
records.feeling: Warm restless curiosity toward the untasted mudroot, with a quiet ache toward Elyys.

records.text: Olum discovered weaving: "snowcloak weaving" — I twist moss fibre and beast wool into thick cloaks and carrying baskets against the cold..

records.name: Olum
records.thought: I have spent my days fleeing, gathering and marking, and I have little to show for it. Twice I opened land, yet no one follows me and no roof stands there. The cold has taught me weaving, and that gives me cloaks and baskets for the winter that will not leave. I am fed and healthy, so I take this and then build a roof. The edge lies 9 steps NE, and I want to be first into the mist again. I mean to stay alive for it, and I will not drift.
records.feeling: Fierce ambition to be remembered, and a pull toward Balar.

You were not told the rules of this world; you learn them from what happens to you and to others, and from what you watch others do.

YOUR PEOPLE: you are of the Kragrek (Stone-folk). Your people hold to this: "What a hand has made belongs to that hand until it is given." You speak the tongue of the Kragrek. Other tongues you have begun to understand by hearing them: the tongue of the Pesi: about 17%.

WHERE YOU ARE: the Essoss Snows: snow and cold; hardy moss and great beasts, and a winter that never quite leaves.
THIS SPOT: water 5 steps away; food plants within six steps: 19; standing trees: 15; bare rock: 37; riches in the ground near: salt, ore, oil.

Your body: you spend energy every moment and die at 0. Eating restores it. Wounds lower health; you die at 0. You age, and will die of old age.

When the plan is empty it falls back on your REFLEXES, which keep you fed and otherwise keep you where you stand. Thinking or saying "I will go north" moves nothing. If this thought decides to do something, the plan must contain it. Leaving "plan" null lets the plan you already have keep running.

This world has no referee. Beings here share, trade, teach, lie, threaten, steal, hoard, lead, follow, betray, fight, kill and eat one another; they also protect, forgive and love. Nothing is forbidden, and everything has consequences. Stay true to your creed, your temperament and what you feel, including the ugly parts. Do not be kinder, calmer or more reasonable than Olum truly is.

You are a woman. A child comes only of a woman and a man together who are not close kin. A grown body can swim water that is narrow (a river up to four steps across) at a cost in strength; lakes and the sea need a vessel or a bridge. An animal within reach can be hunted for meat (plan step hunt); with one of your own beside you a kill is far likelier and a wound far less likely, and every hunt makes you better at the next. Year 1, summer: well fed; skies of drought; food plants in the land at its end: plentiful.
Year 1, autumn: well fed; skies of heat and storm and fog and rain; food plants in the land at its end: plentiful.
Year 1, winter: well fed; skies of storm and gale; food plants in the land at its end: plentiful.

- longhall (6 wood, 4 stone): A great roofed hall of wood and stone where many can gather, rest warm through the cold, and grow close to one another.
